Home / Forex Liquidity / A-Book / B-Book / Hybrid

Meta Grey Label / comparison

A-Book / B-Book / Hybrid

Compare the operating choices, responsibilities and trade-offs before you decide.

Discuss your requirements ↗

Compare models →

Choose your operating model

Control. Scope. Responsibility.

A-Book

Route orders to liquidity providers.

B-Book / Hybrid

Define how selected flow is managed.

Start with what your team needs to manage directly. Confirm the commercial and technical scope before launch.

Explore the decision criteria ↓

The context

Ask any new broker what keeps them up at night and execution often comes up. Not because it’s complicated to set up, but because the choice you make shapes your revenue, your risk and how your clients experience every trade.

The a book vs b book debate has been running in this industry for years, and plenty of people have strong opinions. This page sets out how each model works, the trade-offs involved and why so many brokers now settle on a hybrid. The aim isn’t to tell you which is right. It’s to help you choose with your eyes open.

01 / Explore the detail

What Is A Book Execution?

With a book execution, client orders are passed straight through to your liquidity providers. When a client buys EUR/USD, your broker places a matching trade with the market. You’re the middle person, not the counterparty.

01

How A Book Brokers Make Money

Revenue comes from spread markups and commissions on each trade. Whether the client wins or loses, you earn from their trading activity.

02

The Advantages

There’s no direct conflict of interest, since you don’t profit when clients lose. Your market risk stays low because positions are offset with providers. And some professional traders and institutional clients specifically look for brokers running this model.

03

The Downsides

Margins per trade are thinner. You need decent volumes to build meaningful revenue. Your costs depend on what your liquidity providers charge, and some flow, like aggressive scalping, can be expensive to pass on.

02 / Explore the detail

What Is a B Book Forex Broker?

A b book forex broker keeps client trades in-house rather than sending them to the market. The broker becomes the counterparty. If a client buys, the broker effectively takes the opposite side.

01

How B Book Brokers Make Money

Revenue comes from spreads and commissions, plus net client losses. Statistically, a large share of retail traders lose over time, which is why this model can be profitable.

02

The Advantages

Higher potential revenue per client. No liquidity costs on internalised trades. Faster execution, since orders don’t leave your server.

03

The Downsides

There’s a built-in conflict of interest, because you benefit when clients lose. Profitable traders become a real cost and risk. A run of winning clients, or a sharp market move, can hurt your balance sheet. And regulators in many jurisdictions watch B book practices closely, so transparency and fair treatment are essential.

04

Doing It Responsibly

Running a B book doesn’t have to mean treating clients unfairly. Responsible brokers execute honestly, never manipulate prices, disclose their execution model and keep enough capital to cover exposure. Reputation in this industry travels fast.

03 / Explore the detail

How the Forex Hybrid Model Works

The forex hybrid model combines both approaches. Some client flow goes to liquidity providers. Some stays in-house. The split is decided by rules your dealing team sets.

01

Typical Ways to Split Flow

By client type, so consistently profitable traders are routed out and smaller retail accounts stay internal. By trade size, so large orders go to the market to limit exposure. By instrument, so certain volatile symbols are always hedged. Or by overall exposure, so once internal risk reaches a set level, new trades are passed through.

02

Why Many Brokers Choose Hybrid

It balances revenue with risk. You keep the income potential of internalising some flow, while protecting yourself from the clients and positions that could cause real damage. It’s flexible too, so you can adjust as your client base changes.

03

What It Requires

A hybrid model only works with good data and the right tools. Your dealing team needs to see client behaviour, exposure and profitability clearly, and adjust routing rules confidently.

04 / Explore the detail

A Book vs B Book: Side-by-Side Thinking

Rather than a simple table, it helps to ask a few questions about your own business.

How much capital do you have to absorb risk? A B book needs more. What kind of clients are you targeting? Professional and high-volume traders tend to prefer A book. What do your regulators expect? Some jurisdictions are stricter than others. Do you have an experienced dealing team? B book and hybrid models depend on one. How important is reputation in your market? Transparency carries more weight in some regions than in others.

Your honest answers usually point clearly towards one model or another.

05 / Explore the detail

How We Support Every Execution Model

Whatever model you choose, the technology needs to support it properly.

01

Liquidity Bridge and Routing

We set up your bridge and configure routing rules by group, client, symbol or exposure. Changing the rules later doesn’t require rebuilding anything.

02

Risk Management Tools

Exposure monitoring, client profiling and reporting give your dealing team a clear view of what’s happening in real time.

03

Manager Access on Grey Label and Admin Licences

With a grey label or your own admin licence, you get the control needed to run A book, B book or hybrid execution your way.

06 / Explore the detail

Choose an Execution Model That Fits Your Business

The a book vs b book decision, or the shape of your forex hybrid model, deserves careful thought. It affects your revenue, your risk and your reputation.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

Which model is best for a new brokerage?

Many new brokers start with A book or a cautious hybrid, as it limits risk while they learn their client base. B book requires more capital and experience to manage safely.

Is B book execution legal?

In many jurisdictions it’s permitted, but it often comes with requirements around disclosure, capital and fair treatment of clients. Your legal advisor should confirm what applies to your licence and markets.

Can I change my execution model later?

Yes. Routing rules sit in your bridge and risk tools, so you can shift from A book to hybrid, or adjust your hybrid split, as your business evolves.

Do clients know which model I use?

They should. Many regulators expect brokers to disclose their execution approach, and being open about it builds trust, especially with experienced traders.

Meta Grey Label / company

About Us

The people, principles and technical work behind a connected brokerage.

Discuss your requirements ↗

Compare models →

The context

Every brokerage we’ve helped launch started with someone sitting across the table, slightly overwhelmed. They knew their market. They knew their clients. What they didn’t know was how to get a MetaTrader server live, connected to liquidity, linked to a CRM, and stable enough to trust with real money.

That gap is the reason we exist.

If you’re reading a page about MetaTrader Grey Label, you probably want to know who we are before you trust us with something this important. Fair enough. Here’s the honest picture.

01 / Explore the detail

Who We Are

We’re a forex technology provider that works on one thing: the infrastructure brokers run on. We don’t run a brokerage ourselves, we don’t trade against anyone, and we’re not trying to sell you a dozen unrelated products. Our focus is MetaTrader, and everything we build sits around it.

That focus matters more than it sounds. MetaTrader looks simple from the trader’s side. Behind it, there are server configurations, group settings, bridges, plugins, reports and a long list of things that can quietly go wrong. Our team spends its days inside those details, so you don’t have to.

01

Where We Started

We came into this industry from the technical side. Before MetaGreyLabel, most of us had already spent years setting up servers, fixing bridges and untangling CRM integrations for brokers who’d been let down by vendors. The same complaints came up again and again. Setups took too long. Costs kept creeping up. Support disappeared the moment the contract was signed.

At some point it made more sense to build the service we kept wishing existed.

02

What We Believe

A new broker shouldn’t need a year and a huge budget to get started. They shouldn’t have to manage five suppliers who each blame the others when something breaks. And they should be able to pick up the phone and talk to someone who actually understands the platform.

That’s pretty much the whole philosophy. It isn’t complicated, but it’s surprisingly rare.

02 / Explore the detail

What We Do as a Forex Broker Solutions Company

At its core, we’re a forex broker solutions company that helps people launch and run brokerages without building everything from scratch. Some clients come to us for a single piece of the puzzle. Others want the full package. Both are fine.

01

MetaTrader Grey Label and White Label Setups

This is where most of our clients begin. We set up MT4 or MT5 environments under your brand, with manager access, your own client groups and trading conditions you control. If a lighter white label suits you better for now, we’ll tell you that too.

02

Turnkey Brokerage Packages

For founders starting from zero, we bring everything together. Platform, CRM, client portal, liquidity connections, payment integrations and a branded website, all configured to talk to each other from the first day.

03

Ongoing Technical Support

Launching is the easy bit, honestly. Running a brokerage month after month is where good support earns its keep. We stay involved after go live, handling updates, configuration changes and the odd emergency when markets get busy.

03 / Explore the detail

How We Work With Brokers

We’d rather understand your business properly than rush into a quote. So the first conversation is usually about you. Which markets you’re targeting, what your licensing situation looks like, how many clients you expect in year one, and whether you already have partners in place for payments or liquidity.

From there, we suggest a setup that fits. Sometimes that’s smaller than what the client asked for. We’ve talked plenty of people out of paying for features they won’t need for another year, and we’d do it again.

Once you’re ready, the build moves quickly. Configuration, branding, integrations and testing happen in a tight sequence, and you’re kept in the loop at every step. No disappearing for weeks and coming back with surprises.

01

Straight Answers, Even When They’re Not Exciting

If something will take longer than you hoped, we’ll say so. If a feature won’t work well in your jurisdiction, we’ll say that too. Brokers who’ve been burned before tend to appreciate this more than any sales pitch.

04 / Explore the detail

Why Brokers Stick With Us

Most of our work comes from people who’ve used other providers first. They usually tell us the same things. Our team answers questions properly. Pricing is clear. And when something does go wrong, it gets fixed rather than passed around.

We’re not the biggest name in the industry, and we don’t need to be. As a forex technology provider that sticks to what it knows, we’d rather do a smaller number of things really well than spread ourselves thin.

01

Built to Grow With You

Plenty of our clients start small. A grey label, a basic CRM, one liquidity connection. As they grow, they add more. Better risk tools, more payment options, extra plugins, sometimes a move to a full licence. We plan for that growth from the beginning so nothing has to be torn down and rebuilt later.

02

People You Can Actually Reach

You won’t be handed a ticket number and left to wait. You’ll have direct contacts on our team who know your setup and remember your history. It sounds like a small thing until you need help at a busy market open.

05 / Explore the detail

The People Behind the Platform

Our team is a mix of server engineers, integration specialists, support staff and people who’ve worked inside brokerages themselves. That last group is important. They know what a dealing desk deals with on a volatile day, what compliance teams need from reports, and what frustrates traders enough to make them leave.

Put those perspectives together and you get technology that’s built for how brokerages really work, not how a brochure imagines they do.

06 / Explore the detail

Let’s Talk About Your Brokerage

Whether you’re still sketching out the idea or you’re ready to go live next week, we’re happy to talk it through. Tell us where you are, what you’re trying to build, and what’s been getting in the way.

Choosing a forex broker solutions company is a big decision, and it should feel like a partnership, not a transaction. Now that you know a little more about MetaTrader Grey Label and the people behind it, the next step is simple. Get in touch, and let’s see what we can build together.

The context

Clients see your website, your trading platform and your client portal. They never see the back office. But that’s where your brokerage really runs. Approvals, deposits, withdrawals, compliance checks, partner payouts, reports for management and regulators. If the back office is messy, every other part of the business feels it.

Good forex back office software pulls all of that into one organised system. Your team works faster, mistakes drop, and management gets a clear view of what’s happening across the brokerage without chasing people for updates.

01 / Operational scope

What a Broker Back Office System Handles

A broker back office system is the internal command centre for your operations. Here’s what it typically covers.

01

Client Management

Full client profiles, account details, verification status, communication history and notes, all in one place. Anyone on your team can see the full picture before speaking to a client.

02

KYC and Compliance Review

Review uploaded documents, approve or reject applications, request extra information and record every decision. Your compliance team gets a clear audit trail for every client.

03

Deposits and Withdrawals

See every incoming deposit and outgoing withdrawal request. Approve, reject or hold transactions, check them against payment provider records and make sure balances match MetaTrader.

04

Account Operations

Change leverage, move clients between groups, adjust account settings and handle internal transfers, with changes syncing to MT4 or MT5 automatically.

05

IB and Partner Administration

Approve new partners, assign clients, manage commission plans and process payouts from the same system.

06

Support Tickets

Track client queries, assign them to team members and follow them through to resolution.

02 / Operational scope

The Forex Admin Panel

The forex admin panel is the control layer above everything else. It’s where senior staff manage how the brokerage operates.

01

User Roles and Permissions

Set exactly what each team member can see and do. Sales staff see leads and clients. Support handles tickets. Finance manages payments. Compliance reviews documents. Management sees everything. Nobody has access they don’t need.

02

System Settings

Configure account types, registration requirements, KYC rules, payment methods, email templates and approval workflows without needing a developer.

03

Activity Logs

Every action taken in the system is recorded. Who approved a withdrawal, who changed a client’s leverage, who edited a profile. Useful for internal checks and essential for regulators.

04

Notifications and Alerts

Get notified about large deposits, pending withdrawals, incomplete KYC, unusual activity or anything else your team needs to act on quickly.

03 / Operational scope

Forex Reporting That Actually Helps You Decide

Raw data isn’t much use unless you can make sense of it. Strong forex reporting turns activity across your brokerage into information your team can act on.

01

Financial Reports

Deposits, withdrawals, net funding, payment method performance and balances across all accounts. Your finance team can reconcile quickly and spot problems early.

02

Client Reports

New registrations, verification rates, first-time deposits, active traders and dormant accounts. See where clients drop off and where onboarding could be smoother.

03

Trading Reports

Volumes by symbol, account type, group or region. Understand what your clients actually trade and when.

04

Partner Reports

IB and affiliate performance, client quality by source and commission totals. Decide which partnerships deserve more investment.

05

Sales Reports

Lead sources, conversion rates and individual sales performance, so managers know what’s working and who needs support.

06

Compliance Reports

KYC status across your client base, document expiry dates and records ready for regulatory review.

07

Export and Scheduling

Download reports in common formats or schedule them to arrive automatically, so management gets the numbers without asking.

04 / Operational scope

Why a Connected Back Office Matters

Many brokers start with separate tools for each job. A CRM here, a payment dashboard there, MetaTrader reports somewhere else, and a spreadsheet to tie it all together. It works for a while, but the cracks show quickly.

Balances don’t match. Reports disagree. Staff spend hours copying data between systems. Compliance struggles to prove who did what. When your back office connects directly to MetaTrader, your payment gateways and your client portal, those problems mostly disappear.

05 / Operational scope

Built Into Your Brokerage With Us

With our grey label and turnkey packages, the back office and admin panel come connected to your trading platform, CRM, trader’s room, payments and IB module from day one.

01

Configured to Your Processes

We set up user roles, approval workflows, KYC rules and reports around how your team actually works.

02

Tested Before Launch

Every key process, from client approval to withdrawal to IB payout, is tested end to end so your team starts on solid ground.

03

Training for Your Team

We walk your staff through the system so they’re comfortable from the first day, and we’re on hand for questions after launch.

Whether you’re looking for reliable forex back office software, a flexible forex admin panel, a fully connected broker back office system, or simply better forex reporting, we’ll help you set it up around the way your team works. Get in touch today.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I control what each staff member can access?

Yes. You can create roles with specific permissions, so each team member only sees and does what their job requires.

Does the back office sync with MT4 and MT5?

Yes. Account changes, balances, deposits and withdrawals sync with your MetaTrader server, so records stay consistent across systems.

Can I create custom reports?

You can filter and export reports by date, client group, region, partner and more. If you need something more specific, we can talk through custom reporting options.

Is every action in the back office recorded?

Yes. Activity logs record who did what and when, giving you a clear audit trail for internal reviews and regulators.

07 / Operational scope

Run Your Brokerage From One Clear Command Centre

A well-organised back office makes your whole brokerage easier to run. Fewer errors, faster approvals, better decisions and happier clients.

Brokerage Launch Process

A coordinated path from requirements to a tested environment and managed support.

Discuss your requirements ↗

Compare models →

The context

A reliable brokerage launch is less about a headline timeline and more about sequencing the dependencies correctly. Platform, hosting, liquidity, CRM, KYC and payments need to be planned as one operating system, then tested together before clients arrive.

The technical configuration can move quickly when requirements and third-party approvals are ready. Licensing, banking, liquidity, payment and compliance timelines remain separate dependencies and should be planned honestly from the start.

01 / Explore the detail

01 Discovery

We start with the operating model: target markets, account types, expected volumes, platform preference, execution model and the providers you already have. Clear inputs prevent avoidable rework later.

02 / Explore the detail

02 Architecture

Next we map the stack: MT4 or MT5, hosting region, liquidity connection, CRM, KYC, payments, reporting and the systems that need to exchange data. Existing tools can be retained when they fit the target architecture.

03 / Explore the detail

03 Integration

Platform settings, trading groups, symbols, bridge or gateway connectivity, CRM workflows, KYC and payment services are configured around the approved architecture. Vendor requirements and technical handoffs are coordinated in one implementation plan.

04 / Explore the detail

04 Testing

We test real workflows end to end: onboarding, account creation, deposits, pricing, order routing, rejects, reporting and withdrawals where applicable. The goal is to find integration gaps before a live client does.

05 / Explore the detail

05 Go-Live

Launch happens only after the agreed checks are complete, access has been handed over and monitoring is in place. The team should know how to operate the platform, client systems and escalation path before production traffic starts.

06 / Explore the detail

06 Managed Support

After launch, the environment still needs monitoring, updates, configuration changes, backup checks and incident response. Support continues as the brokerage adds clients, instruments, liquidity routes or operational tools.

07 / Explore the detail

What Affects the Timeline

A standard technical configuration may be short when documents, branding, account structure and provider approvals are ready. Custom websites, unusual integrations, multi-region payment setups, large symbol sets or unresolved licensing and vendor approvals extend the overall timeline.

We separate technical implementation time from external approval time so the launch plan stays realistic.

08 / Explore the detail

What to Prepare Before Implementation

01

Business and market scope

Company details, target jurisdictions, client profile, intended account types and expected launch sequence.

02

Platform and trading decisions

MT4, MT5 or both; instruments; leverage and group structure; execution model; liquidity preference; and any migration requirements.

03

Operational dependencies

CRM, KYC, payment providers, domains, branding, reporting requirements and the status of any regulatory or banking approvals.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

Can the technology be configured quickly?

Yes, when the scope is standard and the required inputs are ready. The full brokerage launch can still take longer because licensing, liquidity, payment, banking or compliance approvals are outside the platform configuration itself.

What usually causes delays?

Incomplete requirements, missing documents, unfinished branding, unresolved provider approvals, custom integrations and late changes to account or execution models are common causes.

Will the full workflow be tested before go-live?

That is the target. Platform, integrations, reporting and client operations should be tested together against the agreed scope before production launch.

Does Meta Grey Label handle regulatory approval?

No. We provide technology, software and infrastructure integration. Regulatory, legal and licensing obligations remain with the brokerage and its qualified advisers.

Common Mistakes to Avoid When Choosing a MetaTrader Grey Label Provider

Practical perspectives on brokerage technology and operations.

5 min read · Meta Grey Label

The context

Switching grey label providers is possible, but it’s never pleasant. You’re moving client accounts, trade history, configurations and integrations, usually while trying to keep the brokerage running as if nothing is happening. Most brokers who go through it say the same thing afterwards: we should have asked more questions at the start.

This piece is about those questions. Below are the metatrader grey label mistakes we see most often, and what to do differently.

01 / Explore the detail

Mistake 1: Choosing on Price Alone

It’s understandable. Launch budgets are tight, and when one provider quotes noticeably lower than the others, it’s tempting to stop looking.

The trouble is that headline prices hide a lot. A low setup fee might come with volume charges that rise sharply as you grow. A cheap monthly fee might leave out the backup server, extra manager terminals or plugin support. Some providers make their margin on add-ons you only find out about once you’re committed.

What to do instead: ask every provider for an estimated total cost at launch, after twelve months and at your target volume. Compare those totals, not the opening quote.

02 / Explore the detail

Mistake 2: Not Checking Who Holds the License

Your grey label runs under someone else’s MetaQuotes license. If that license is shaky, so is your brokerage.

Some providers are resellers of resellers, several steps removed from the actual license holder. That’s not always a problem, but it adds risk and often slows down support, because every serious issue has to go up the chain.

Ask directly who holds the master license, how long they’ve held it, and what your position is if anything changes. If the answer is vague, treat that as your answer.

03 / Explore the detail

Mistake 3: Assuming “Admin Access” Means Full Control

Most grey label providers advertise admin access. Not all of them mean the same thing by it.

Some lock certain settings. Others restrict which plugins you can install, or insist all changes go through their team. You may only find out when you try to configure something and it’s greyed out.

Before you sign, ask for a written list of anything you won’t be able to change yourself. Better still, ask for a test login to the admin terminal and look around.

04 / Explore the detail

Mistake 4: Ignoring What Happens If You Leave

Nobody likes planning for a breakup at the start of a relationship. But this one matters.

Find out:

Whether you’ll get a full export of client data and trade history

In what format, and how quickly

Whether there are exit fees or long notice periods

What happens to your server name and branding

A provider confident in their service won’t make leaving difficult. One that dodges these questions probably relies on lock-in to keep clients.

05 / Explore the detail

Mistake 5: Underestimating Support Needs

On a quiet Tuesday afternoon, support barely matters. On a Sunday night before the market opens, with your server not responding, it’s the only thing that matters.

Many brokers accept “24/7 support” at face value. In practice, that can mean a ticketing system someone checks the next morning. Ask what live monitoring is in place, what the response times are for critical issues, and whether those times are in the contract.

Then test it. Send a few technical questions during the sales process, including one late at night or on a weekend, and see what comes back.

06 / Explore the detail

Mistake 6: Overlooking Integration Experience

Your MetaTrader server has to work with your bridge, CRM, payment gateways, risk tools and reporting. If the provider hasn’t connected those particular tools before, you’re paying for their learning curve.

When you choose metatrader grey label provider partners, ask which bridges, CRMs and liquidity providers they’ve already integrated on live servers. Ask for examples, not just a general “we support everything”. Real experience means fewer surprises in your first weeks.

07 / Explore the detail

Mistake 7: Picking Server Location Without Thinking

Server location affects execution. If your server is on one continent and your liquidity provider on another, every order carries extra latency. Traders notice, especially scalpers and EA users.

Some providers offer one location and don’t mention it unless asked. Make sure you know where your server will be, whether you can choose, and how close it is to your main liquidity source.

08 / Explore the detail

Mistake 8: Skipping Reference Checks

Sales calls show you the best version of a provider. Other brokers show you the real one.

Ask for two or three current clients you can speak to, ideally ones similar in size to your brokerage. Ask about their worst outage, how quickly it was fixed, whether fees have changed since they joined, and whether they’d sign again.

If a provider won’t give you any references, that tells you something.

09 / Explore the detail

Mistake 9: Rushing the Decision

Providers sometimes push a deadline: a discount ending Friday, limited server slots, a promotion for new brokers. Occasionally that’s genuine. More often it’s meant to stop you comparing.

Your grey label will likely sit at the centre of your brokerage for years. An extra week of checking won’t hurt your launch. A rushed choice might hurt everything after it.

10 / Explore the detail

Mistake 10: Not Thinking About Growth

What works for 200 clients may not hold up at 5,000. Before signing, ask how the provider handles growth. Can your server be upgraded easily? Will pricing change sharply at higher volumes? Can you add more servers, more plugins or new platforms later?

Choosing for where you’ll be in two years saves you a migration in eighteen months.

11 / Explore the detail

A Simple Checklist Before You Sign

Total cost estimated at three stages of growth

Master license holder confirmed and checked

Written list of any admin restrictions

Clear exit terms and data export process

Support response times written into the contract

Proof of integration with your chosen tools

Server location agreed

At least two reference calls completed

If a provider passes all eight, you’re in good shape.

12 / Explore the detail

Conclusion

Most metatrader grey label mistakes come from taking things on trust that should have been checked. None of these checks take long, and each one protects you from a much bigger problem later.

When you’re ready to choose metatrader grey label provider support for your brokerage, MetaGreyLabel is happy to go through this checklist with you, point by point.

Brokerage insights

Comparing MetaTrader Grey Label Providers: Features, Support and Prices

Practical perspectives on brokerage technology and operations.

5 min read · Meta Grey Label

The context

On paper, most grey label providers look almost the same. Dedicated server, admin access, branded terminals, round-the-clock support. Read five websites back to back and you’d struggle to tell them apart.

The differences show up later. They appear when your server slows down during a news spike, when you need a plugin installed urgently, or when you find a fee in month three that nobody mentioned. So when brokers ask us about the best metatrader grey label providers, the honest answer is that it depends less on the brochure and more on what happens once you’re live.

Here’s how to compare providers properly, beyond the sales pitch.

01 / Explore the detail

Start With the Basics: Are They Legitimate?

Before you look at features or price, check the foundation. A grey label runs under your provider’s master MetaQuotes license. If their license has problems, so do you.

Ask how long they’ve held the license and whether it’s in good standing. Ask how many brokers they currently host and how long their oldest clients have been with them. A provider that’s been around for years with brokers who stay is a far safer bet than one with flashy pricing and no track record.

Also find out what happens if the provider runs into trouble. Can your server and client data be moved? Is there a clear exit process? You’d hope never to need it, but you want the answer before you sign.

02 / Explore the detail

Comparing Features

When you compare metatrader grey label offers, set up a simple table and score each provider against the same list. It stops one impressive feature from distracting you from gaps elsewhere.

01

Server and Infrastructure

Which platforms they offer: MT5 only, or MT4 as well where it’s still possible

Where they can host your server, and whether you get to choose

Whether a backup server is included or charged separately

How failover works if the main server goes down

Who handles MetaQuotes updates and how quickly they’re rolled out

02

Access and Control

Check that you’re actually getting full administrator access, not a limited admin role with some settings locked. Some providers quietly restrict what you can change. Ask directly which settings you can’t touch.

Also find out how many manager terminals are included. A growing dealing desk, support team and back office can need more than you’d think.

03

Integrations and Plugins

Find out which bridges, CRMs, risk tools and liquidity providers they’ve already integrated. A provider with tested connections saves you weeks of troubleshooting. One that says “we can integrate anything” without examples may be learning on your server.

Ask too whether you can bring your own tools, or whether they push you towards their in-house products.

03 / Explore the detail

Comparing Support

Support is where providers differ most, and where it’s hardest to judge before you sign.

01

What to Ask

What hours is technical support actually available, including weekends before the market opens?

Is there live monitoring of your server, or do they only respond once you report a problem?

What are their response times for urgent issues, and are they written into the agreement?

Will you have a named account manager, or will each ticket go to whoever is free?

Do they help with configuration, such as setting up groups and symbols, or is that entirely on you?

02

How to Test It

Don’t just take their word for it. Send a few technical questions before signing and see how quickly and clearly they reply. Ask for references from current brokers, and actually call them. Ask those brokers about the worst problem they’ve had and how the provider dealt with it. That one answer will tell you more than any sales call.

04 / Explore the detail

Comparing Prices

Grey label pricing is rarely as simple as one monthly number. Providers bundle and split costs in different ways, so lining up headline prices side by side can mislead you.

01

Common Cost Elements

One-time setup fee

Monthly server and license fee

Charges per active account, or based on trading volume

Backup server fees

Extra manager terminals

Plugin and integration costs

Charges for custom development or configuration work

02

Reading Between the Lines

A low setup fee sometimes comes with high volume-based charges, which can get expensive once you start growing. A higher flat fee might work out cheaper over two or three years. Ask each provider to estimate your total cost at three points: at launch, at your expected volume after a year, and at a stretch target. That gives you a far more honest comparison than the opening price.

Also check the contract length and notice period. A cheap deal that locks you in for three years with a heavy exit fee isn’t really cheap.

05 / Explore the detail

Red Flags to Watch For

A few warning signs come up again and again:

Pricing that changes depending on who you speak to

Vague answers about who actually holds the MetaQuotes license

No clear process for moving your data if you leave

Pressure to sign quickly because of a “limited offer”

Reluctance to put you in touch with existing clients

Support contacts that turn out to be a single email address

Any one of these is worth questioning. Several together usually mean walking away.

06 / Explore the detail

Matching the Provider to Your Brokerage

The best metatrader grey label providers for a new broker aren’t necessarily the best for an established one. If you’re just starting, you might value hands-on configuration help and a simple, predictable fee. If you’re already running volume, deep integrations, strong risk tools and solid uptime guarantees matter more.

Be honest about where you are now and where you expect to be in a year. Pick the provider that fits that path, not the one with the longest feature list.

07 / Explore the detail

Conclusion

When you compare metatrader grey label providers, look past the website and test what matters: the license behind the service, the support you’ll get when things go wrong, and the full cost over time. A careful week of comparison can save you a painful migration later.

If you’d like to see how our setup measures up against your checklist, MetaGreyLabel is happy to answer the hard questions and connect you with brokers already running on our servers.

Brokerage insights

Compliance and KYC Basics for MetaTrader Grey Label Brokerages

Practical perspectives on brokerage technology and operations.

6 min read · Meta Grey Label

The context

Compliance rarely makes it into the exciting part of a brokerage launch. Nobody gets into forex because they love writing AML policies. But it’s the part that decides whether you keep your license, keep your bank accounts and keep your payment processors. Get it wrong and it doesn’t matter how good your platform is.

A grey label gives you a lot of control over your trading environment. That control comes with responsibility. Here are the basics every grey label brokerage should have in place, and how your technology can make the job easier.

01 / Explore the detail

First, Know Where the Responsibility Sits

Your grey label provider runs the MetaTrader server under their master license. But they’re not your compliance department. Your regulatory obligations belong to your brokerage, the licensed entity dealing with clients.

That covers knowing who your clients are, monitoring their activity, keeping proper records and reporting suspicious behaviour. The provider supplies tools and data. You decide how to use them and you answer for the results.

It’s worth making this clear in your own planning from day one. metatrader grey label compliance is about your processes as much as your technology.

02 / Explore the detail

What KYC Actually Involves

Know Your Customer is the process of confirming who your clients are before and during your relationship with them. Requirements vary by jurisdiction, but most forex broker kyc processes include a few core pieces.

01

Identity Verification

Clients usually provide a government-issued photo ID, such as a passport, national ID card or driving licence. Many brokers add a selfie or liveness check to make sure the person uploading the document is the person on it.

02

Proof of Address

A recent utility bill, bank statement or official letter showing the client’s name and address. Most regulators expect this document to be no more than a few months old.

03

Appropriateness or Suitability Checks

Many regulators require you to assess whether trading leveraged products suits a client. This usually means a short questionnaire on trading experience, financial knowledge and sometimes income and savings. Clients who lack experience may get warnings, lower leverage, or in some cases be declined.

04

Source of Funds and Wealth

For larger deposits, or clients flagged as higher risk, you may need to understand where their money comes from. That could mean payslips, tax returns, business records or other supporting documents.

03 / Explore the detail

AML: Keeping Watch After Onboarding

KYC confirms who someone is when they join. Anti-money laundering work continues for as long as they’re a client.

Your AML programme should cover:

Screening clients against sanctions lists and politically exposed person databases

Monitoring deposits and withdrawals for unusual patterns

Checking that withdrawals go back to the same source the funds came from where possible

Watching for third-party payments, where someone else funds a client’s account

Reporting suspicious activity to the relevant authorities

Common warning signs include large deposits followed by little or no trading and a quick withdrawal, frequent changes in payment methods, accounts linked to the same device or IP address, and clients who resist providing documents.

04 / Explore the detail

Risk-Based Approach

Not every client needs the same level of checks. Most regulators expect a risk-based approach, where you apply more scrutiny to higher-risk clients and keep things simpler for lower-risk ones.

Factors that often raise a client’s risk level include:

Living in, or sending funds from, higher-risk countries

Being a politically exposed person or closely linked to one

Very large or unusual deposit amounts

Complex ownership structures for corporate accounts

Write your risk categories down, apply them consistently and review them regularly. Regulators care a lot about whether your process is documented and actually followed.

05 / Explore the detail

Record Keeping

You’ll need to keep KYC documents, transaction records and communication logs for a set number of years, often five or more, depending on your jurisdiction. Records need to be secure, organised and quick to retrieve if a regulator or auditor asks.

This is one area where a grey label really helps. Your trading data sits on your own dedicated server instead of a shared one, which makes it simpler to pull complete, accurate records for your own clients.

06 / Explore the detail

How Technology Supports Compliance

Good tools won’t make you compliant on their own, but they make the work far more manageable.

01

CRM and Client Portal

Your CRM should handle document uploads, track verification status and store everything in one place with a clear audit trail. Clients should be able to see what’s still needed, and your team should be able to approve or reject documents with notes explaining why.

02

Automated Verification

Third-party ID verification services can check documents, compare selfies and screen against sanctions lists in seconds. They clear straightforward cases quickly and pass unclear ones to your compliance team.

03

Trading and Transaction Monitoring

Because you have admin access to your grey label server, you can set up monitoring that looks at actual trading behaviour. That might flag accounts depositing large sums without trading, linked accounts making opposite trades, or patterns that suggest abuse of bonuses or IB programmes.

04

Regulatory Reporting

Many regulators expect periodic reports on client funds, trading activity or capital. Back office tools that pull data directly from your MetaTrader server save hours of manual work and reduce the risk of mistakes.

07 / Explore the detail

Common Compliance Mistakes

A few problems come up again and again with new brokerages:

Letting clients trade before verification is complete, to avoid losing sign-ups

Accepting low-quality documents because checking takes time

Inconsistent decisions, where similar clients are treated differently

Missing withdrawal checks, especially for third-party payment methods

Policies that exist on paper but aren’t actually followed day to day

Each of these can lead to fines, lost banking relationships or worse. Payment processors are often stricter than regulators, and losing one can freeze your business overnight.

08 / Explore the detail

Balancing Compliance and Client Experience

Strict compliance doesn’t have to mean a frustrating sign-up. The best brokers make it feel smooth:

Explain clearly why each document is needed

Allow uploads from mobile in a few taps

Use automated checks to approve simple cases quickly

Keep clients updated on their status instead of leaving them waiting

Ask for extra documents only when there’s a real reason

Clients will accept checks they understand. What drives them away is confusion and silence.

09 / Explore the detail

Conclusion

Solid forex broker kyc and AML processes protect your license, your banking partners and your reputation. A grey label gives you the server control and data access to support those processes properly, but the policies, decisions and accountability stay with you. Work with a compliance specialist familiar with your jurisdiction, and build your systems around their advice.

If you’d like to see how your grey label setup can support your metatrader grey label compliance workflow, MetaGreyLabel can show you the tools and integrations available.

Brokerage insights

Copy Trading and Social Trading for MetaTrader Grey Label Brokers

Practical perspectives on brokerage technology and operations.

6 min read · Meta Grey Label

The context

A lot of people are curious about trading but have no intention of learning chart patterns or sitting in front of a screen during the London open. They have money, interest and a phone. What they don’t have is time or confidence.

Copy trading speaks directly to them. It lets clients follow experienced traders automatically, and it gives those experienced traders a way to earn from their skill. For brokers, it opens the door to an audience that would never sign up for a standard trading account.

If you run a MetaTrader grey label, you’re well placed to offer it properly. Here’s how it works and what to think about before you launch.

01 / Explore the detail

Copy Trading vs Social Trading

The two terms get used interchangeably, but there’s a small difference worth knowing.

Copy trading is the mechanism. A follower links their account to a strategy provider, and trades are copied automatically in proportion to the follower’s balance and chosen settings.

Social trading is the wider experience around it. Leaderboards, trader profiles, performance stats, comments, ratings and community features that help followers decide who to trust.

Most modern platforms combine both. The copying engine does the work, and the social layer helps clients choose.

02 / Explore the detail

Why It Matters for Your Brokerage

Becoming a copy trading broker brings several practical benefits:

A wider audience. You reach passive investors as well as active traders.

More trading volume. One successful strategy provider can generate trades across hundreds of follower accounts.

Better retention. Followers who see steady results tend to stay longer and add funds.

A new kind of partner. Strong strategy providers bring their own audiences, much like introducing brokers.

Something to market. Leaderboards and success stories give you real content to promote.

It isn’t right for every brokerage, but for many it becomes one of the main reasons clients choose them over competitors.

03 / Explore the detail

Why Grey Label Makes a Difference

Copy trading systems sit closely alongside your MetaTrader server. They need to read trades from strategy accounts and place matching trades on follower accounts almost instantly.

On a white label, whether you can offer copy trading, and which system you can use, is usually up to the host. With a grey label, you have admin access to your own server, so you choose the copy trading solution, configure it the way you want, and connect it to your CRM and client portal.

That control shows up in the details. A good metatrader grey label copy trading setup lets you decide which groups can provide or follow strategies, how fees are calculated, how quickly trades are copied, and what risk limits apply.

04 / Explore the detail

Key Features to Look For

01

Flexible Copying Options

Followers should be able to choose how they copy. Common settings include copying in proportion to balance, using a fixed lot size, or applying a multiplier. They should also be able to set limits, such as a maximum drawdown that automatically stops copying.

02

Clear Performance Data

Followers make decisions based on what they can see. Strategy profiles should show returns over different periods, maximum drawdown, average trade length, instruments traded, number of followers and how long the strategy has been running. The more honest and complete the data, the better the decisions, and the fewer complaints later.

03

Fee Structures for Strategy Providers

Strategy providers need a reason to share their trades. Typical options include:

Performance fees, a share of the profits generated for followers

Subscription fees, a fixed monthly charge

Volume-based rewards, a rebate per lot traded by followers

Management fees, a small percentage of the funds following them

Your system should calculate and pay these automatically, with clear statements for both providers and followers.

04

Fast, Reliable Copying

Speed matters. If a follower’s trade opens several seconds after the provider’s, the results can differ noticeably, especially in fast markets. Ask any copy trading vendor how they handle latency, partial fills and slippage between master and follower accounts.

05

Mobile Access

Many followers will manage everything from their phones. They should be able to browse strategies, start or stop copying and check results without needing a desktop.

05 / Explore the detail

Risks You Need to Manage

Copy trading brings real benefits, but also real risks. Handle them carefully.

01

Reckless Strategy Providers

Some providers chase short-term returns with very high risk. A strategy can look brilliant for three months and then wipe out followers in an afternoon. Consider minimum track record requirements, risk scores on profiles, and caps on leverage or drawdown for strategies shown on public leaderboards.

02

Misleading Performance Claims

Followers need to understand that past results don’t guarantee future ones. Display risk warnings clearly, show drawdown as prominently as returns, and avoid marketing that implies guaranteed profits.

03

Regulatory Considerations

In some jurisdictions, offering copy trading can be viewed as portfolio management or investment advice, which may require extra permissions. Check with your compliance adviser before launch. The rules differ widely from one regulator to another.

04

Execution and Risk on Your Side

When one provider has hundreds of followers, a single trade can turn into a large combined position on your book. Your risk tools and liquidity setup need to handle that. Many brokers route copy trading flow differently from regular retail flow for exactly this reason.

06 / Explore the detail

Getting Strategy Providers on Board

A copy trading platform is only as good as the strategies on it. A few ways to attract solid providers:

Reach out to experienced traders already on your platform with consistent results

Partner with trading educators and signal providers who already have followers

Offer fair, transparent fee structures and pay on time

Give top providers visibility through featured profiles and marketing support

Set quality standards so good providers aren’t lost in a crowd of reckless ones

Some brokers also run competitions on demo or small live accounts to find promising traders early.

07 / Explore the detail

Launching Without Overcomplicating Things

You don’t need every feature on day one. A sensible first version might include:

A copying engine connected to your grey label server

A simple leaderboard with honest performance stats

One or two fee structures for providers

Clear risk warnings and copying limits for followers

Integration with your client portal so everything sits in one place

Add community features, advanced filters and more fee options once you see how clients actually use it.

08 / Explore the detail

Conclusion

Becoming a copy trading broker can bring in new clients, raise volumes and give you a strong edge in a crowded market, provided you manage risks, set fair rules and keep performance data honest. Running your own metatrader grey label copy trading setup gives you the control to do that properly.

If you’re thinking about adding copy trading to your brokerage, MetaGreyLabel can help you choose a solution and connect it to your existing setup.

The context

Mobile and web trading are convenient, but when traders want to do real work, they sit down at a desktop. That’s where they run multiple charts side by side, build and test strategies, leave expert advisors trading overnight and dig into the detail behind every decision.

For your most active and valuable clients, the desktop platform is where they live. Offering a reliable MT4 desktop terminal and MT5 desktop terminal, branded with your name, tells those traders your brokerage is built for them.

01 / Explore the detail

Why the Desktop Platform Still Matters

01

Your Most Active Traders Use It

Clients who trade often, trade larger volumes or run automated strategies almost always rely on the desktop terminal. They tend to generate a big share of a brokerage’s trading activity.

02

The Full Toolkit Lives Here

Custom indicators, expert advisors, scripts, the strategy tester and advanced chart layouts all work best, and in many cases only work, on desktop.

03

Bigger Screen, Better Decisions

Multiple monitors, detailed charts and several instruments open at once. Desktop gives traders the space to analyse properly.

02 / Explore the detail

MT4 Desktop Terminal

The MT4 desktop terminal remains one of the most widely used trading tools in the world, especially among forex traders.

01

What Traders Get

Nine timeframes, a wide range of built-in indicators and drawing tools, one-click trading, multiple chart windows and full support for custom indicators and expert advisors written in MQL4.

02

Why Traders Stay Loyal

Many traders have spent years building or buying MT4 tools. Their entire trading routine depends on them. Offering MT4 on desktop lets these clients move to your brokerage without giving anything up.

03

Best Suited For

Forex-focused traders, long-time MT4 users and those who rely on established EAs and indicators.

03 / Explore the detail

MT5 Desktop Terminal

The MT5 desktop terminal builds on everything MT4 offers and adds more depth for modern, multi-asset trading.

01

What Traders Get

Twenty-one timeframes, more built-in indicators and analytical objects, additional order types, market depth on supported instruments, a built-in economic calendar and support for MQL5 expert advisors and indicators.

02

A Faster Strategy Tester

MT5’s multi-threaded strategy tester can test EAs across multiple currencies and use real tick data, making it far quicker and more accurate than MT4’s. Algo traders notice this straight away.

03

Multi-Asset Trading

Forex, metals, energies, indices, stocks, futures and crypto CFDs can all be traded from one terminal, depending on what your brokerage offers.

04

Best Suited For

Multi-asset traders, algorithmic traders and newer clients who want the most current MetaTrader experience.

04 / Explore the detail

Branded Desktop Trading Platform

Your clients should know who they’re trading with every time they open their platform. A branded desktop trading platform keeps your brokerage front and centre.

01

Your Name on the Installer

Clients download the platform from your website through an installer carrying your company name. Your server is pre-set, so they don’t have to search for it.

02

Your Brand Inside the Terminal

Your company name appears in the platform and your server name shows at login, reinforcing your brand every session.

03

Easy Downloads From Your Website

We help you set up clear download links for Windows and guidance for Mac users, so clients get up and running without needing support.

04

What’s Available Depends on Your Setup

The level of branding you can apply depends on whether you’re on a white label, grey label or your own admin licence. We’ll explain exactly what’s possible with your chosen model.

05 / Explore the detail

Desktop Features Traders Value Most

01

Expert Advisors

Automated trading strategies can run continuously, opening and managing trades based on pre-set rules.

02

Custom Indicators and Scripts

Traders can install their own tools or choose from thousands available in the MetaTrader community.

03

Strategy Tester

Test and optimise trading strategies on historical data before risking real money.

04

Multiple Chart Layouts

Save and switch between chart setups for different strategies or markets.

05

Signals and Copy Trading

Depending on your setup, traders can subscribe to trading signals or follow other traders directly from the terminal.

06 / Explore the detail

Part of a Complete Platform Offering

Desktop works best alongside web and mobile. Traders often analyse and set up trades on desktop, then monitor and manage them from their phone or browser during the day. With one account working across every device, positions and balances stay in sync wherever they log in.

With our white label, grey label and turnkey setups, desktop access is configured together with your web and mobile platforms, linked from your website and trader’s room, and tested before you go live.

07 / Explore the detail

Give Your Serious Traders the Tools They Need

Your most active clients judge you by the platform they spend hours on each day. A dependable MT4 desktop terminal and MT5 desktop terminal, set up properly and carrying your brand, helps you win and keep those traders.

If you’re ready to offer a branded desktop trading platform as part of your brokerage, we’ll help you set it up and get it into your clients’ hands quickly. Get in touch today.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the desktop terminal work on Mac?

MetaTrader is built for Windows, but Mac users can run it using available Mac versions or compatibility tools. We’ll help you provide clear instructions for Mac clients.

Can traders use the same account on desktop, web and mobile?

Yes. One set of login details works across all devices, and everything stays in sync.

Can clients run MT4 EAs on MT5?

Not directly. MT4 expert advisors are written in MQL4 and need to be rewritten in MQL5 to run on MT5. If many of your clients rely on MT4 tools, offering both platforms is often the easiest solution.

Will the desktop platform carry my branding?

Yes, to the extent your setup allows. We’ll explain exactly what branding is available with your white label, grey label or admin licence.

Brokerage insights

Essential Tools and Plugins for a MetaTrader Grey Label Brokerage

Practical perspectives on brokerage technology and operations.

6 min read · Meta Grey Label

The context

Getting your own MetaTrader server is a big step. But on its own, a server is just an engine with no dashboard. What actually makes a brokerage run day to day is the set of tools and plugins sitting around it: the ones that route orders, flag risky clients, move money, and keep your regulator satisfied.

The good news with a grey label is that you get to pick those tools yourself. The less fun news is that it’s easy to overspend on extras you won’t touch for a year, or to launch without something you’ll badly need in week two. Here’s how to think about it.

01 / Explore the detail

Why Plugins Matter More on a Grey Label

On a white label, the host decides which add-ons run on the server, and you live with whatever they’ve picked. On a grey label, you have admin access, so you choose and configure your own stack. That freedom is a large part of the appeal, but it also means the job of choosing well now lands on you.

The right metatrader grey label plugins can mean the difference between a brokerage that runs itself most days and one where your team is fixing problems by hand at 2 a.m.

02 / Explore the detail

The Non-Negotiables

Some tools aren’t really optional. If you’re missing any of these at launch, you’ll notice quickly.

01

A Liquidity Bridge

This is the piece that connects your MetaTrader server to your liquidity providers. It takes client orders and sends them to the market, or routes them internally if you run a B-book or hybrid model.

When comparing bridges, look at execution speed, how many liquidity providers it can connect to at once, how flexible the routing rules are, and how much visibility you get into each fill. A good bridge lets you send larger or more toxic flow one way and smaller retail flow another, without someone having to step in manually.

02

A Forex CRM

Your CRM is where clients sign up, pass KYC, deposit, withdraw and manage their accounts. It’s also where your sales and support teams spend most of the day. It needs to sync properly with MetaTrader so accounts, balances and groups update automatically.

Pay attention to the client portal as well. Traders judge your brokerage by it more than you’d expect. If it’s slow or confusing, they assume your execution will be too.

03

Payment Gateway Integrations

You’ll want several ways for clients to fund their accounts: bank wire, cards, local payment methods, perhaps crypto where it’s allowed. Most of these connect through your CRM rather than straight to MetaTrader, but they belong on your list from day one. Clients who can’t deposit easily simply go somewhere else.

03 / Explore the detail

Risk Management Tools

This is the category new brokers tend to underestimate, and it’s where a lot of money is quietly lost or saved.

A proper risk tool gives your dealing desk a live view of exposure by symbol, by client and by group. It should flag unusual behaviour such as latency arbitrage, scalping on stale prices, or one client opening positions across several linked accounts.

Some brokers also add specialist plugins for:

Detecting toxic flow and moving those clients to A-book automatically

Setting exposure limits that adjust hedging as positions grow

Protecting against price spikes and bad ticks

Monitoring negative balances and handling them

If you run any B-book, risk tools aren’t a nice extra. They’re part of the core setup.

04 / Explore the detail

Back Office and Reporting

Regulators want reports, and so do your accountants. MetaTrader’s built-in reporting covers the basics, but most brokers outgrow it fast.

A back office tool pulls data from your server into clean reports on trading volume, deposits, P&L by group, IB commissions and so on. If you’re regulated, look for tools that can produce reports in the format your regulator expects. Building those by hand every month is miserable, and that’s when mistakes start to creep in.

05 / Explore the detail

Tools That Help You Grow

Once the basics are working, these are the forex broker tools that tend to bring in clients and keep them.

01

Copy Trading and PAMM/MAM

Copy trading lets less experienced clients follow successful traders automatically. PAMM and MAM systems let money managers trade on behalf of several investors from one master account. Both are popular, both increase volume, and both bring in clients who wouldn’t otherwise trade at all.

They do add complexity though, especially around fees, payouts and compliance. It’s worth waiting until your core operation runs smoothly before adding them.

02

IB and Affiliate Management

Introducing brokers are a major source of clients for many brokerages. An IB module tracks referrals, calculates rebates across multiple levels and pays out commissions without someone wrestling a spreadsheet every week. If IBs are part of your growth plan, get this in early. They notice errors in their payouts very quickly.

03

Extra Trading Tools for Clients

Things like advanced charting packages, trading signals, economic calendars and one-click trading add-ons. They aren’t essential, but they give your marketing team something to talk about and make your offering feel more complete than a bare terminal.

06 / Explore the detail

How to Choose Without Overbuying

It’s tempting to launch with everything. Resist that. Each plugin adds cost, setup time and one more thing that can break.

A sensible approach is to split your stack into three layers:

Launch essentials: bridge, CRM, payments, basic risk monitoring

First few months: reporting, IB module, stronger risk tools

Once you’re growing: copy trading, PAMM/MAM, extra client tools

Before you commit to any plugin, ask a few plain questions. Does it actually work with your MetaTrader version? Who supports it if something goes wrong at midnight? How is it priced, flat fee, per account or by volume? And can you switch it off or replace it later without rebuilding everything?

07 / Explore the detail

Integration Is the Real Test

One thing experienced brokers learn the hard way: a plugin that looks great in a demo can still be a headache if it doesn’t play nicely with the rest of your stack. Your CRM, bridge, risk tools and reporting all need to share data cleanly. When they don’t, you end up with mismatched balances, duplicate accounts and reports nobody trusts.

That’s why it often pays to work with a provider who has already tested common combinations of metatrader grey label plugins on live servers, rather than piecing together tools from five vendors who’ve never met.

08 / Explore the detail

Conclusion

The best stack isn’t the biggest one. It’s the one that fits your execution model, your markets and your team’s capacity right now, with room to add more later. Start with the essentials, get them working properly, then build out as your client base grows.

If you’re working out which forex broker tools make sense for your launch, MetaGreyLabel can help you put together a setup that suits where your brokerage is today.

Fx Company & License

Find the right components for your brokerage. Explore the options, then define a connected operating model.

The context

Before your first client places a trade, a lot has to happen behind the scenes. You need a company. You may need a licence. You’ll need bank accounts, payment partners and liquidity providers who are willing to work with you. And every one of those depends on getting the legal foundation right.

For many founders, this is the most confusing part of starting a brokerage. The rules differ from country to country, the paperwork is heavy and the wrong early decision can cost a lot to undo. This page explains how forex company formation and licensing usually work, what choices you’ll face and how we help you bring it all together with your technology.

Choose your next step

Explore Fx Company & License

Offshore Company Formation

Many brokers don’t start in London, Sydney or New York. They start offshore. It’s often quicker, more affordable and far less complicated than…

Explore Offshore Company Formation ↗

01 / Explore the detail

Why the Legal Structure Matters So Much

Your company and licence affect almost everything that comes after.

01

Where You Can Accept Clients

Your licence, or lack of one, decides which countries you can legally serve. Some markets are open to brokers from many jurisdictions. Others only allow locally regulated firms.

02

Which Partners Will Work With You

Banks, payment providers and liquidity providers all look closely at your company structure and licensing before they agree to work with you.

03

How Clients See You

Many traders check whether a broker is regulated before they deposit. A credible licence builds trust and can make marketing easier.

04

Your Ongoing Costs and Obligations

Different jurisdictions come with different capital requirements, reporting rules and compliance responsibilities.

02 / Explore the detail

Forex Company Formation: The First Step

Setting up your company is usually where everything begins.

01

Choosing a Jurisdiction

The right location depends on your target markets, budget, timeline and long-term plans. A business aiming at clients across emerging markets may choose differently from one targeting professional traders in Europe.

02

Registering the Company

This involves preparing documents, appointing directors and shareholders, setting up a registered office and completing local registration requirements.

03

Opening Corporate Bank Accounts

Brokers often find banking one of the harder steps. Banks want to understand your business model, ownership and compliance approach before opening accounts.

04

Preparing for Licensing

If you plan to apply for a licence, your company structure, management team and policies need to meet the regulator’s requirements from the start.

03 / Explore the detail

Offshore Forex Company Options

An offshore forex company is a common starting point for new brokers, particularly those targeting international clients outside the strictest regulatory regimes.

01

Why Brokers Choose Offshore

Offshore jurisdictions often offer lower setup costs, simpler requirements, lower minimum capital and faster timelines than major financial centres.

02

The Trade-Offs

Some banks, payment providers and clients prefer brokers with stronger regulation. Certain markets don’t allow offshore brokers to solicit their residents at all. It’s important to understand where you can and can’t operate.

03

A Stepping Stone for Many

Plenty of brokers start offshore, build their client base and revenue, then add a licence in a more established jurisdiction as they grow.

04 / Explore the detail

Understanding the Forex Broker License

A forex broker license is permission from a financial regulator to offer trading services. What it involves depends heavily on the regulator.

01

Different Levels of Regulation

Some regulators are known for strict requirements, high capital levels and close supervision. Others offer lighter-touch frameworks. Each sends a different signal to clients and partners.

02

What Regulators Typically Look For

Common requirements include minimum capital, fit and proper directors, a physical presence or local staff, AML and KYC policies, client fund segregation, risk management procedures and regular reporting.

03

Timelines Vary Widely

Some licences can be obtained in a few months. Others take a year or more. Planning around this from the beginning saves a lot of frustration.

04

Get Proper Legal Advice

Licensing is a legal matter, and requirements change. Always work with qualified legal advisors who specialise in financial services in your chosen jurisdiction.

05 / Explore the detail

MetaTrader Grey Label Company License: Bringing It All Together

A company and licence are only part of the picture. You still need trading technology, client systems and payments that match your legal setup. That’s where a MetaTrader grey label company license approach helps, aligning your legal structure and your technology from day one.

01

Technology That Fits Your Licence

KYC rules, client restrictions by country, reporting requirements and onboarding questions are configured in your CRM and back office to match what your licence requires.

02

Documents Partners Expect

Liquidity providers, payment processors and banks often ask about your trading technology. Having a proper grey label setup in place can make those conversations smoother.

03

Launch Ready When Your Licence Is

While your company and licence are being finalised, we can prepare your platform, CRM and integrations, so you can go live soon after approval.

06 / Explore the detail

How We Help

We focus on the technology side of your brokerage, but we understand how closely it’s tied to your legal setup.

01

Planning Support

We’ll talk through your target markets and business model, and help you think about how your licensing choices affect your technology and partners.

02

Introductions to Licensing Partners

We can point you towards legal and corporate service providers experienced in forex company formation and licensing.

03

Compliance-Ready Setup

Your CRM, KYC module, client portal and reporting tools are configured around your licence requirements.

Whether you’re starting with forex company formation, considering an offshore forex company, preparing for a forex broker license, or planning a full MetaTrader grey label company license setup, we’ll help you connect your legal plans with technology that’s ready to go. Get in touch today.

The context

Your trading platform gets all the attention, but the CRM is where your brokerage actually runs. It’s where clients sign up, where documents get checked, where deposits are recorded and where your sales and support teams spend most of their day.

A clunky CRM slows everything down. Clients get stuck in onboarding. Deposits go missing between systems. Your team spends hours fixing records by hand. A well-built forex CRM and trader’s room take all of that off your plate, so your people can focus on clients rather than admin.

01 / Explore the detail

What a Forex CRM Does for Your Brokerage

A forex CRM is the operating system for your business. It connects your clients, your team and your trading platform in one place.

01

Client Onboarding

Registration forms, email verification, document uploads and approval workflows. New clients move from sign-up to funded account without endless back and forth.

02

KYC and Compliance

Collect ID and proof of address, track verification status, flag incomplete profiles and keep a clear audit trail for your compliance team and regulators.

03

Sales and Lead Management

Track leads from first contact to first deposit. Assign them to sales staff, log calls and notes, and see which campaigns actually bring in funded clients.

04

Client Support

Keep every client’s history in one place. Accounts, deposits, withdrawals, tickets and conversations, so your support team can help quickly without digging through emails.

05

Reporting

Deposits, withdrawals, client activity, sales performance and IB commissions, all in clear reports your management team can actually use.

02 / Explore the detail

The Forex Trader’s Room

The forex trader’s room is the part of your CRM your clients see. It’s their personal space for managing everything outside of trading itself.

01

Account Management

Clients can open new live or demo accounts, change leverage where you allow it and view all their accounts in one dashboard.

02

Deposits and Withdrawals

Funding and withdrawals happen directly in the trader’s room, connected to your payment gateways. Requests flow straight to your back office for approval.

03

Internal Transfers

Clients can move funds between their own trading accounts without contacting support.

04

Documents and Profile

Upload verification documents, update personal details and track KYC status, all from one place.

05

Your Branding Throughout

The trader’s room carries your logo, colours and domain. To your clients, it’s simply part of your brokerage.

03 / Explore the detail

What to Look For in Forex Broker CRM Software

There’s a lot of forex broker CRM software on the market. These are the features that tend to matter most once you’re live.

01

Proper MetaTrader Sync

This is the big one. Accounts, balances, deposits and trading data need to sync with MT4 and MT5 accurately and in real time. If they don’t, your team ends up fixing mismatches every day.

02

Payment Gateway Integration

Deposits should credit trading accounts automatically once confirmed. Withdrawals should follow clear approval steps. Manual processing is slow and error prone.

03

IB and Affiliate Management

Track introducing brokers and affiliates, assign clients to partners, set commission structures and calculate payouts automatically. Partners should be able to see their own reports too.

04

Role-Based Access

Sales, support, compliance, finance and management need different views and permissions. Good CRM software lets you control exactly who sees and edits what.

05

Multi-Language Support

If you serve clients in several regions, both the CRM and trader’s room should support the languages your clients use.

06

Automation

Welcome emails, KYC reminders, deposit confirmations and inactivity follow-ups should run on their own, without your team setting them up one by one.

04 / Explore the detail

MetaTrader Grey Label CRM: Built to Work Together

If you’re launching with us, the MetaTrader grey label CRM comes connected to your platform from day one. You’re not left trying to make two separate systems talk to each other.

01

Pre-Integrated and Tested

Your CRM is linked to your MT4 or MT5 grey label, your payment gateways and your IB module before launch. We test every client journey end to end.

02

Configured Around Your Business

Onboarding steps, KYC requirements, account types, approval workflows and user roles are set up to match how your brokerage operates.

03

Room to Grow

Start with the essentials, then add more advanced features as your team and client base grow. Copy trading, PAMM, extra payment methods and more languages can all be added later.

05 / Explore the detail

Already Have a CRM?

If you’re happy with a CRM you already use, we can connect it to your MetaTrader setup rather than replacing it. If it’s causing problems, we can help you migrate client data to a better system with minimal disruption.

06 / Explore the detail

Give Your Team and Clients a Better Experience

The right forex CRM makes your brokerage easier to run and easier to trust. Clients onboard faster, deposits land properly and your team spends its time on people rather than paperwork.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the CRM work with both MT4 and MT5?

Yes. The CRM connects to MT4, MT5 or both, so clients can open and manage accounts on either platform from the same trader’s room.

Can clients deposit and withdraw directly in the trader’s room?

Yes. Once your payment gateways are integrated, clients can fund and withdraw from their accounts directly. Your team approves requests through the back office.

Can I customise the onboarding and KYC steps?

Yes. We configure registration fields, document requirements and approval workflows to suit your licence and target markets.

Can my IBs see their own reports?

Yes. The IB module gives partners their own portal where they can track referred clients, trading volumes and commissions.
