The context

There’s a point most growing brokers hit. The business is working, clients are coming in, and suddenly the limits of a basic setup start to hurt. You want to change spreads for a particular group and can’t. You want to manage your own risk and need permission first. You want to move faster than your provider allows.

That’s usually when a forex grey label starts to make sense. You keep the cost advantages of running on an existing MetaTrader server, but you get the controls that let you run your brokerage the way you actually want to.

Choose your next step

Explore Forex Grey Label

MT4 Grey Label

MT4 has outlasted a lot of predictions. Every few years someone says it’s on the way out, and every year millions of traders keep opening it each…

Explore MT4 Grey Label ↗

MT5 Grey Label

Today’s traders rarely stick to one market. The same client might trade EUR/USD before breakfast, gold at lunch and the Nasdaq in the evening. If…

Explore MT5 Grey Label ↗

Grey Label Pricing

A grey label is a bigger step than a white label, so it makes sense that brokers want to understand the numbers properly before committing. The…

Explore Grey Label Pricing ↗

Upgrade Grey Label to Admin License

A grey label is a great place to grow. You’ve got your brand, your own groups and real control over trading conditions. But at some point, many…

Explore Upgrade Grey Label to Admin License ↗

01 / Explore the detail

What Is a Forex Grey Label?

A grey label sits between a white label and a full MetaTrader licence. Your brokerage runs on a server that’s already licensed, hosted and maintained, but unlike a white label, you get your own manager access and much greater independence over how your business operates.

You decide your trading conditions. You build your own groups. Your team monitors exposure and manages clients directly. The heavy infrastructure work, like hosting, updates and server stability, stays with us.

01

Think of It Like This

A white label is like leasing a shop in a mall where management sets your opening hours and decides what you can stock. A grey label is more like leasing your own building. Someone else still owns the land and keeps the lights on, but inside, you run things your way.

02 / Explore the detail

What You Control as a Grey Label Forex Broker

Running as a grey label forex broker gives you a level of control that white label setups simply don’t offer.

01

Trading Conditions

Set your own spreads, markups, commissions, swaps and leverage. Adjust them by client group, account type or region. If you want a tighter offer for high-volume traders and a standard one for retail, you can do it.

02

Groups and Symbols

Create and manage your own account groups. Choose which instruments each group can trade and how they’re configured. Add new symbols as your product range grows.

03

Risk Management

This is where a grey label really earns its place. You decide how client flow is handled, how much goes to liquidity providers and how different groups are treated. For brokers serious about building revenue, that flexibility is hard to give up once you’ve had it.

04

Manager and Admin Terminals

Your dealing team gets proper manager terminal access. They can watch positions in real time, react to market moves and handle client issues without waiting on an outside team.

03 / Explore the detail

MetaTrader Grey Label: Grey Label Setups Built Around Your Business

When brokers ask us about a MetaTrader grey label, grey label setups usually come with a lot of confusion about what’s included. So here’s what ours covers.

You get a branded MetaTrader environment carrying your company name, configured groups and symbols, manager and admin access, back office tools and connection to your liquidity bridge. Depending on your package, we can also add a forex CRM, client portal, payment integrations, IB module and a branded website.

Everything is set up and tested together before you go live, so the platform, CRM and payments all talk to each other properly from day one.

04 / Explore the detail

MT4 MT5 Grey Label Options

We offer MT4 MT5 grey label setups, so you can choose the platform that suits your traders or run both.

01

MT4 Grey Label

Ideal if your audience is mostly forex traders attached to their MT4 indicators and expert advisors. It’s familiar, stable and still widely used across many markets.

02

MT5 Grey Label

The better fit if you plan to offer indices, commodities, stocks or crypto CFDs alongside forex. MT5 also offers more timeframes, better order handling and a faster strategy tester, which algo traders appreciate.

03

Running Both Platforms

Many brokers offer both, letting traders pick what they prefer. It widens your audience and means you never lose a client over platform choice.

05 / Explore the detail

Who a Grey Label Suits Best

A grey label works best for brokers who already have some traction. White label brokers who’ve outgrown their restrictions. Introducing brokers with strong volumes who want to run their own book. Established firms launching a new brand in a fresh region. Founders with experienced dealing and compliance staff who want flexibility from the start.

If you’re still testing whether your market will respond, a white label may be the cheaper starting point. We’ll tell you honestly which fits better.

06 / Explore the detail

Why Brokers Choose Our Grey Label Service

Plenty of providers offer grey labels. What clients tell us they value is the support behind ours. Our team knows MetaTrader at the server level, so when something needs fixing during a busy session, you’re speaking with someone who can actually sort it out.

Pricing is laid out clearly before you sign, with no extra charges creeping in later. And because we work only on MetaTrader infrastructure, it’s the thing we’re best at, rather than one product among many.

01

Growing Beyond a Grey Label

When your volumes eventually justify a full licence, we’ll help you plan that move too. Our aim is to support your brokerage through each stage, not just the first one.

07 / Explore the detail

Ready to Take Control of Your Brokerage?

If you’ve outgrown a basic setup, or you want independence from day one, a forex grey label gives you the controls you need without the cost of a full licence.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

How is a grey label different from a white label?

Both let you trade under your own brand on an existing server. A grey label adds manager access and much greater control over trading conditions, groups and risk, while a white label keeps more of those settings under the main server’s oversight.

How long does a grey label setup take?

Once your documents and branding are ready, a standard setup can go live within a few days. More complex configurations, like running both MT4 and MT5 or adding several integrations, can take a little longer.

Can I move from a white label to a grey label later?

Yes, and many of our clients do exactly that. Because both run on our infrastructure, we move your groups and client accounts across with minimal disruption to your traders.

Do I need my own liquidity provider?

You’ll need liquidity connected to your setup, and we can integrate the providers you already work with. If you don’t have one yet, we can point you towards options that suit your size and markets.

Forex Liquidity

Find the right components for your brokerage. Explore the options, then define a connected operating model.

Discuss your requirements ↗

Compare models →

The context

Clients rarely think about liquidity until something goes wrong. A trade fills at a strange price. Spreads blow out during a news release. An order sits there longer than it should. Then suddenly liquidity is the only thing they care about, and they’re quietly comparing you with other brokers.

Good liquidity is what makes a brokerage feel solid. Tight spreads, fast execution and fills that hold up when markets move. We help brokers connect to the right forex liquidity providers for their size and markets, and set up the technology that keeps it all running smoothly.

Choose your next step

Explore Forex Liquidity

A-Book / B-Book / Hybrid

Ask any new broker what keeps them up at night and execution often comes up. Not because it’s complicated to set up, but because the choice you make…

Explore A-Book / B-Book / Hybrid ↗

Liquidity Bridge

Most traders will never hear the word “bridge.” They’ll just notice whether their orders fill quickly and at the price they expected. Behind every…

Explore Liquidity Bridge ↗

Prime of Prime (PoP)

Every broker wants the deep, tight pricing that big banks offer. Very few can get it directly. Tier 1 banks typically ask for large capital deposits,…

Explore Prime of Prime (PoP) ↗

01 / Explore the detail

What Liquidity Actually Means for a Broker

In simple terms, liquidity is the supply of prices and the ability to fill orders at those prices. When your client clicks buy on EUR/USD, someone has to be on the other side. Liquidity providers are the banks, non-bank market makers and institutions that supply those prices.

The quality of your liquidity shapes almost everything your traders experience. Spread width, execution speed, slippage, how many symbols you can offer and how your platform behaves when markets get busy.

01

Why It Affects Your Revenue Too

Better pricing attracts and keeps more traders. Smoother execution means fewer complaints and fewer clients leaving. And the way you manage liquidity, how much flow you route out and how much you keep, directly affects your margins.

02 / Explore the detail

Tier 1 Liquidity for Brokers: What It Really Means

You’ll see tier 1 liquidity for brokers advertised everywhere. It’s worth understanding what that actually involves.

01

Who Tier 1 Providers Are

Tier 1 usually refers to the largest global banks and top non-bank market makers. They offer deep pricing and strong reliability across major currency pairs.

02

How Most Brokers Access It

Here’s the part some providers don’t explain. Tier 1 banks typically only deal directly with very large institutions. Most brokers access that pricing through prime-of-prime providers, who aggregate liquidity from several tier 1 sources and offer it to smaller firms with lower capital requirements.

That’s not a bad thing. For most growing brokers, a good prime-of-prime relationship gives access to deep pricing without the enormous deposits and credit requirements of going direct.

03

Ask the Right Questions

When a provider claims tier 1 liquidity, ask where it actually comes from, how many sources are aggregated and what their execution statistics look like. Honest providers will answer clearly.

03 / Explore the detail

MetaTrader Grey Label Liquidity Setup

If you’re running a grey label with us, MetaTrader grey label liquidity is connected as part of your setup. You don’t have to figure out the integration yourself.

01

Liquidity Bridge Connection

A liquidity bridge links your MetaTrader server to your providers. It passes client orders out, brings prices in and handles execution in milliseconds. We configure and test the bridge so it works reliably from day one.

02

Bring Your Own Providers

Already have relationships with liquidity providers? We’ll connect them. If you’re starting fresh, we can point you towards providers suited to your size, markets and budget.

03

Multiple Providers, One Feed

Many brokers connect more than one provider. Aggregation lets you combine their pricing, pick the best available quote and keep trading if one source has problems.

04 / Explore the detail

Our Forex Liquidity Solutions

Our forex liquidity solutions cover more than plugging in a price feed. We look at the whole picture, from connection to risk management.

01

Provider Selection Support

We help you compare options based on your client profile, volumes, instruments and target regions. A broker serving retail forex traders in Asia needs something different from one offering indices to professional clients in Europe.

02

Bridge and Aggregation Setup

We configure your bridge, set up aggregation across providers and tune it for speed and stability.

03

Multi-Asset Liquidity

If you’re offering more than forex, we can help connect liquidity for metals, energies, indices, stocks and crypto CFDs, particularly on MT5.

04

Execution and Risk Settings

You decide how flow is handled. A-book, B-book or a hybrid approach, routing rules by group or client type, and exposure limits. We set up the tools so your dealing team can manage it confidently.

05

Monitoring and Support

Once live, we keep an eye on connections, latency and execution quality. If a feed drops or something behaves oddly, our team is there to help sort it out.

05 / Explore the detail

Choosing the Right Liquidity Setup

There’s no single best answer. The right setup depends on your stage.

New brokers often start with one solid prime-of-prime provider and a simple routing model. As volumes grow, many add a second provider, introduce aggregation and refine their routing. Larger brokers may eventually negotiate direct relationships with bigger institutions.

We’ll help you choose what fits now and plan for what comes next, without pushing you into a more complex setup than you need.

06 / Explore the detail

Get Liquidity That Holds Up When It Matters

Your traders judge you on execution, often without realising it. Choosing the right forex liquidity providers and setting them up properly is one of the best investments a brokerage can make.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need my own liquidity provider to launch?

Yes, your brokerage needs liquidity connected before you go live. If you don’t have a provider yet, we can recommend options and help you through onboarding.

Can I connect more than one liquidity provider?

Yes. Multiple providers can be aggregated through your bridge, giving you better pricing and backup if one source has an issue.

What deposit do liquidity providers usually require?

It varies widely depending on the provider, the instruments and your expected volumes. Prime-of-prime providers usually have far lower requirements than going direct to a tier 1 bank.

Can I switch liquidity providers later?

Yes. Because the bridge sits between your platform and your providers, you can add, remove or change providers without rebuilding your brokerage.

The context

Not every new brokerage needs its own server on day one. In fact, most don’t. If you’re testing a market, building a client base or simply want to keep your early costs down, a forex white label is often the smartest way to begin.

You get a working trading platform under your own brand, connected and ready for clients, without spending a fortune on licences and infrastructure. We handle the technical side. You focus on bringing in traders.

Choose your next step

Explore Forex White Label

MT4 White Label

Some platforms come and go. MetaTrader 4 has stuck around for close to two decades, and there’s a simple reason. Traders know it, trust it and have…

Explore MT4 White Label ↗

MT5 White Label

Traders want more than currency pairs these days. They want gold in the morning, US indices in the afternoon and maybe a few stocks or crypto CFDs on…

Explore MT5 White Label ↗

White Label Pricing

Pricing is usually the first thing brokers want to know and the last thing most providers explain clearly. You’ll often see “contact us for a quote”…

Explore White Label Pricing ↗

White Label vs Grey Label

Ask ten people in this industry to explain the difference and you’ll probably get ten slightly different answers. Some providers use the terms…

Explore White Label vs Grey Label ↗

01 / Explore the detail

What Is a Forex White Label?

Think of it as renting a fully furnished office instead of building one from the ground up. The building, the wiring and the security already exist. You move in, put your name on the door and start working.

With a white label, your brokerage runs on an existing MetaTrader server that’s already licensed and maintained. Your clients log in to a platform carrying your brand, your logo and your company name. Behind the scenes, the heavy lifting is handled for you.

01

How It Works in Practice

We set up a branded MT4 or MT5 terminal for your clients, create your trading groups and connect everything to a back office you can manage. You decide how you market yourself, which clients you go after and how you build relationships with them. The server, updates and core maintenance stay with us.

02

Who It’s Built For

A white label works especially well for introducing brokers ready to move beyond earning rebates, first-time founders who want to prove their model before investing heavily, and established businesses adding forex to an existing financial offering. If you want to get trading quickly without a large upfront commitment, it’s a natural place to start.

02 / Explore the detail

Why Start as a White Label Forex Broker?

Starting as a white label forex broker gives you something every new business needs: room to learn without betting everything on day one.

01

Much Lower Upfront Costs

A full MetaTrader server licence is a serious investment, and that’s before hosting, integrations and staff. A white label strips most of that away. Your money can go into marketing, compliance and building a team instead.

02

Faster Time to Market

Because the infrastructure already exists, setup is quick. Once your paperwork and branding are ready, you can be welcoming clients far sooner than if you were building your own stack.

03

Less Technical Burden

You don’t need in-house server engineers or a dedicated IT team. Updates, stability and maintenance sit with us, which leaves you free to run the business side.

03 / Explore the detail

MT4 MT5 White Label: Which Platform Should You Offer?

Both platforms have loyal followings, and our MT4 MT5 white label options let you offer either one, or both side by side.

01

MT4 White Label

MT4 is still hugely popular, especially with forex traders who’ve used it for years and rely on their favourite indicators and expert advisors. If your target audience leans experienced and forex focused, MT4 can make onboarding much easier.

02

MT5 White Label

MT5 is the newer platform and supports a wider range of instruments, including stocks, indices, commodities and futures. It also offers more timeframes, better order handling and stronger testing tools. Most new brokers now lean towards MT5, particularly if they plan to offer more than currency pairs.

03

Offering Both

Plenty of brokers run both platforms so traders can choose what they’re comfortable with. It widens your audience and removes one more reason for a prospective client to look elsewhere.

04 / Explore the detail

What’s Included in Your White Label Setup

A platform alone doesn’t make a brokerage. Clients need to sign up, verify their identity, fund their accounts and get help when something goes wrong. Depending on your package, your setup can include a branded trading platform on MT4, MT5 or both, a forex CRM with KYC checks and a client portal, payment gateway integrations for cards, bank transfers and crypto, an IB module for managing partners and commissions, and a branded website and trader’s room.

Each piece is connected and tested before you go live, so data flows properly from the moment your first client signs up.

05 / Explore the detail

MetaTrader Grey Label White Label: Knowing the Difference

People often mix these two up, and it’s worth getting clear on before you commit. Our MetaTrader grey label white label options sit on the same infrastructure, but they give you different levels of control.

01

White Label

Lower cost, quicker setup and minimal technical responsibility. The trade-off is less control over things like spreads, risk settings and some group configurations, which remain under the main server’s oversight.

02

Grey Label

More independence. You get manager access, your own groups and much greater say over trading conditions. It costs more than a white label but far less than a full licence.

03

Moving Up When You’re Ready

Many clients start on a white label and upgrade to a grey label once their volumes and team grow. Because both run within our setup, the move is straightforward and your clients won’t notice any disruption. The flexibility of a MetaTrader grey label white label path means you never have to rebuild from scratch.

06 / Explore the detail

Why Brokers Choose Our White Label Service

There are plenty of providers offering a forex white label, so here’s what we do a bit differently.

We’re upfront about costs, so there’s no stream of add-on charges after you sign. Our support team knows MetaTrader properly and can sort out real problems rather than passing you between departments. And we’re honest when a white label isn’t the right fit. If a grey label would suit your plans better, we’ll tell you, even if it means a different conversation.

07 / Explore the detail

Start Your Brokerage the Simple Way

Launching a brokerage doesn’t have to mean months of setup and a huge budget. With the right partner, you can get your brand in front of traders quickly, keep costs under control and grow at a pace that makes sense.

Ready to become a white label forex broker with a setup you can trust? Tell us about your plans, your target markets and whether you’d like an MT4 MT5 white label or one platform to start. We’ll come back with a clear proposal and a realistic timeline. Get in touch today.

Grey Label Pricing

Understand setup, ongoing service and optional modules before choosing your scope.

Discuss your requirements ↗

Compare models →

The context

A grey label is a bigger step than a white label, so it makes sense that brokers want to understand the numbers properly before committing. The trouble is, most providers keep pricing vague until you’re deep into a sales call.

This page does the opposite. It explains what goes into a grey label forex price, how setup and monthly fees work, where the costs can rise and how to keep them under control. By the end, you should have a realistic sense of your budget before speaking to anyone.

01 / Explore the detail

Why a Grey Label Costs More Than a White Label

It’s a fair question. Both run on existing MetaTrader infrastructure, so why the price gap?

The answer is control. With a grey label, you get your own manager and admin access, independent groups, custom trading conditions and much more say over risk. That means more server resources, more configuration work and more hands-on support from our side. You’re paying for independence, and for most growing brokers, it pays for itself fairly quickly.

01

Still Far Below a Full Licence

To keep things in perspective, a grey label remains a fraction of what a full MetaTrader server licence costs once you add hosting, integrations and an in-house technical team. You get much of the freedom without that weight.

02 / Explore the detail

How Grey Label Pricing Is Structured

Your total cost comes down to three parts.

01

The Setup Fee

A one-time payment that covers getting you live. Server configuration, manager and admin access, branding, groups and symbols, liquidity bridge connection, CRM and payment integrations if included, and full testing with your team.

02

The Grey Label Monthly Fee

The grey label monthly fee covers keeping everything running. Server access and hosting, platform updates, routine configuration changes, monitoring and support from people who know MetaTrader properly. It’s fixed and agreed before you sign.

03

Optional Add-Ons

Extra tools you can add when you’re ready. Copy trading, PAMM and MAM, additional payment gateways, advanced risk plugins or a second platform. None of these are required at launch.

03 / Explore the detail

Our Grey Label Packages

Most brokers fit into one of the packages below. Each can be adjusted to suit your plans.

01

Essential Grey Label

Setup fee: [price] Monthly fee: [price]

A branded MT4 or MT5 grey label with manager and admin access, configured groups and symbols, liquidity bridge connection and standard support. Ideal for brokers moving up from a white label.

02

Professional Grey Label

Setup fee: [price] Monthly fee: [price]

Everything in Essential, plus a forex CRM with KYC, a trader’s room, payment gateway integration, an IB module and priority support. Our most popular choice for brokers with steady client volumes.

03

Complete Grey Label

Setup fee: [price] Monthly fee: [price]

A full brokerage in one package. Grey label platform, CRM, client portal, multiple payment gateways, IB module, branded website and dedicated account contacts. Built for firms that want one partner handling all of it.

04 / Explore the detail

MT4 Grey Label Pricing Compared With MT5

Brokers often assume MT4 grey label pricing is very different from MT5. In practice, the gap between the two platforms is usually modest.

What moves the price more is everything around the platform. The number of symbols, how many groups you need, which integrations you add and whether you want both platforms running together.

01

When MT4 Is the Better Value

If your traders are mainly forex focused and rely on MT4 indicators and EAs, an MT4 grey label keeps them happy and keeps your setup simple.

02

When MT5 Is Worth It

If you plan to offer indices, commodities, stocks or crypto CFDs, MT5 handles everything in one place. Paying for MT5 now usually works out cheaper than migrating later.

05 / Explore the detail

Is There Such a Thing as a Cheap Forex Grey Label?

Yes and no. You’ll find providers advertising a cheap forex grey label at prices that look almost too good. Sometimes they’re genuine. More often, the low headline figure is followed by extra charges for reports, plugins, configuration changes or support hours.

01

What to Check Before You Sign

Ask exactly what the monthly fee covers. Ask whether routine changes cost extra. Ask what support looks like at 2am during a market spike. And ask for every fee in writing. A cheap offer that can’t answer these clearly usually ends up costing more.

02

How We Keep Costs Low Without Cutting Corners

We price our packages so new grey label brokers can afford them, and we only include what you’ll actually use. Start lean, then add tools as your volumes grow. Your costs scale with your revenue rather than running ahead of it.

06 / Explore the detail

Costs Outside Your Grey Label

To budget properly, you’ll also need to plan for third-party costs. Licensing and company registration, legal and compliance advice, liquidity provider deposits or fees, payment processor charges and marketing. These don’t come from us, but we’d rather you know about them now.

07 / Explore the detail

Get a Clear Grey Label Quote

Working out your grey label forex price shouldn’t feel like a guessing game. Share your plans with us and we’ll give you a straight, itemised answer.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I start on a smaller package and upgrade later?

Yes. Many brokers start with our Essential package and move up as their client base grows. Upgrades are straightforward and don’t require rebuilding your setup.

Does the monthly fee change as my brokerage grows?

Your fee is fixed for the package you choose. If your client numbers grow well beyond what was planned, or you add new tools, we’ll discuss any change with you before it happens.

Are configuration changes included?

Routine changes like adjusting spreads, adding groups or updating symbols are covered by your monthly fee. Larger projects, such as a new integration, are quoted separately so you can decide.

How do I get an exact quote?

Tell us your target markets, expected client numbers, preferred platform and the features you need. We’ll send a detailed proposal with every cost listed.

Brokerage insights

How MetaTrader Grey Label Can Help You Attract More Forex Traders

Practical perspectives on brokerage technology and operations.

6 min read · Meta Grey Label

The context

Every broker says they offer tight spreads, fast execution and great support. Traders have heard it so often that it barely registers anymore. What actually wins clients these days is harder to fake: how the platform feels when they place a trade, how quickly a withdrawal arrives, and whether the account types fit how they really trade.

Most of that comes down to how much control you have over your setup. That’s where a grey label starts to earn its keep. It won’t market your brokerage for you, but it gives you the tools to build an offer that makes it far easier to attract forex traders and hold on to them.

01 / Explore the detail

Traders Already Know MetaTrader

Start with the obvious point. MetaTrader is the platform most retail traders learned on. They know where everything is, they have their favourite indicators set up, and many of them run Expert Advisors they’ve spent months tuning.

Ask them to switch to an unfamiliar platform and plenty will simply say no. Offer MetaTrader with your brand on it and you’ve removed one of the biggest reasons not to sign up. A grey label gives you exactly that, on a server that’s yours rather than one shared with a dozen other brokers.

02 / Explore the detail

Better Execution Is a Selling Point You Can Prove

Traders talk. On forums, in Telegram groups, on YouTube, they compare slippage, requotes and fill speeds between brokers. A reputation for poor execution spreads quickly and is hard to shake off.

With a grey label, you choose your own liquidity providers and configure your own bridge. That means you can:

Work with liquidity providers whose pricing and depth actually suit your clients

Route orders in a way that keeps fills clean

Host your server close to your liquidity to cut latency

Change providers if quality drops, instead of putting up with whatever a host offers

When your execution is genuinely good, you can show it. Publish execution stats, offer a demo that reflects real conditions, and let traders judge for themselves. Experienced traders trust that more than any slogan.

03 / Explore the detail

Account Types That Fit Different Traders

A scalper, a swing trader and a beginner on a small deposit all want different things. On a white label, you’re often limited to the account structures the host allows. On a grey label, you build them yourself.

01

Ideas That Tend to Work

A raw spread account with commission for active traders and EA users

A standard account with no commission and slightly wider spreads for newer clients

Swap-free accounts for traders who need them

Cent or micro accounts for people testing the water with small amounts

Different leverage options depending on regulation and client experience

Being able to tune each group, its margin levels, commissions, swaps and symbol list, lets you shape offers for specific audiences rather than one generic product that suits nobody especially well.

04 / Explore the detail

Features That Bring in New Kinds of Clients

Some traders don’t want to trade on their own at all. Others want to earn from their skills by managing money for followers. A grey label lets you add tools that reach these groups.

01

Copy Trading and Social Features

Copy trading appeals to people who are curious about forex but don’t have the time or confidence to trade themselves. They pick a strategy provider, set a risk level and let it run. For your brokerage, it’s a way to reach a much wider audience than active traders alone.

02

PAMM and MAM for Money Managers

Successful traders often want to manage funds for others. Giving them proper PAMM or MAM tools turns them into partners who bring their own investors with them. One good money manager can bring more volume than months of paid ads.

03

Partner and IB Programmes

Introducing brokers remain one of the most reliable ways to grow forex brokerage volume. With a grey label, you can connect a proper IB system with clear multi-level rebates and automated payouts. IBs stay loyal to brokers who pay accurately and on time, and they’re quick to leave the ones who don’t.

05 / Explore the detail

Trust Is a Growth Tool

Traders have become more cautious, and they’re right to be. They want to know their money is safe and that the broker isn’t working against them.

A grey label helps here in a few quiet ways. Your client data sits on your own server, not a shared one. You can show regulators and partners a cleaner, more transparent setup. And with your own branding on every terminal, your brokerage looks established rather than like a reseller of someone else’s platform.

None of that replaces proper regulation or honest marketing. But it supports both.

06 / Explore the detail

Fast Payments Keep Traders Around

This one isn’t strictly about MetaTrader, but it’s closely connected. With a grey label, your CRM and payment systems link directly to your own server, so deposits show up quickly and withdrawals can be processed without a host sitting in the middle.

Slow withdrawals are among the top reasons traders leave a broker and warn others away. Fast, predictable payouts do the opposite. Happy clients refer their friends, and that’s the cheapest acquisition channel there is.

07 / Explore the detail

Using Your Setup in Your Marketing

Having a strong platform only helps if people hear about it. A few ways brokers put their grey label setup to work:

Run demo competitions on your own server, with real prizes and leaderboards

Publish monthly execution reports showing average spreads and fill speeds

Create content around specific account types for specific trader groups

Feature successful strategy providers from your copy trading platform

Give IBs branded materials and tracking links that make promoting you easy

Each of these depends on having control over your server and your data, which is exactly what a grey label provides.

08 / Explore the detail

Where Growth Really Comes From

The brokers who manage to attract forex traders consistently aren’t usually the ones with the biggest ad budgets. They’re the ones whose product holds up when traders start using it. Clean execution, sensible account options, reliable withdrawals and useful tools turn first deposits into long-term clients.

A grey label won’t fix a weak business plan. But for brokers serious about building something lasting, it removes many of the limits that stop a brokerage from offering what traders want.

09 / Explore the detail

Conclusion

If you want to grow forex brokerage volume in a market this crowded, your platform has to be part of the pitch. Control over execution, accounts and features gives you something real to talk about, and something traders will notice once they’ve signed up.

If you’re looking at how a grey label could support your growth plans, MetaGreyLabel can help you map out a setup built around the traders you want to reach.

Brokerage insights

How Much Capital Do You Need to Start With MetaTrader Grey Label?

Practical perspectives on brokerage technology and operations.

6 min read · Meta Grey Label

The context

It’s usually the first question new brokers ask, and the most frustrating to answer, because the honest reply is “it depends”. But it doesn’t depend on mystery. It depends on a handful of decisions you can make up front: where you’re regulated, how you plan to execute trades, and how quickly you want to grow.

Once those are clear, working out your forex broker startup capital becomes far more manageable. Here’s how to break it down.

01 / Explore the detail

The Grey Label Itself Is Rarely the Biggest Cost

This surprises a lot of people. They expect the platform to eat most of the budget, then discover it’s often one of the smaller line items.

A grey label costs a fraction of a full MetaQuotes license, which is a big part of its appeal. You’ll usually pay a one-time setup fee and then a monthly fee for the server, license and maintenance. Some providers also charge by number of accounts or trading volume.

Prices vary a lot between providers, so get written quotes from a few. When you build your metatrader grey label budget, plan for at least twelve months of platform fees, not just the setup cost. Running out of money in month six because you only budgeted for launch is a very common way for new brokerages to fail.

02 / Explore the detail

Regulation Is Usually Where the Big Money Goes

Your regulatory route drives your total capital needs more than anything else.

01

Minimum Capital Requirements

Every regulator sets a minimum amount of capital your company must hold. These range from relatively modest sums in some offshore jurisdictions to hundreds of thousands of euros or more with stricter European and tier-one regulators. The figure often depends on the type of license too. A broker that holds client positions on its own book is usually required to hold more than one that only passes orders through.

This money isn’t spent, but it is locked up. You can’t use it for marketing or salaries.

02

Setup and Ongoing Compliance

On top of the capital itself, there are legal fees, application fees, local office or director requirements, audits, compliance officers and annual renewal costs. In stricter jurisdictions, these can easily outweigh the platform costs several times over.

Talk to a specialist lawyer before you settle your budget. The jurisdiction you pick will reshape every other number in your plan.

03 / Explore the detail

Technology Beyond the Platform

A grey label gives you the trading server. You’ll still need to pay for the rest of your stack.

Liquidity bridge: connects your server to liquidity providers, usually with a setup and monthly fee

Forex CRM and client portal: handles onboarding, KYC, deposits and withdrawals

Risk management tools: essential if you run any B-book flow

Website and hosting: your brand’s front door

Back office and reporting tools: especially if your regulator expects detailed reporting

Some grey label providers bundle a few of these together, which can save money and integration headaches. Check the cost of each piece individually so you know what you’re really paying for.

04 / Explore the detail

Liquidity and Execution Costs

If you’re running A-book, many liquidity providers ask for a deposit or margin before they’ll give you access. The amount depends on the provider and your expected volume, but it’s money you need to set aside before launch.

If you plan to run B-book or hybrid, you’ll need enough capital to absorb client wins. A few lucky traders in your first month can make a serious dent if your balance sheet is thin. This is one of the most overlooked parts of startup capital, and one of the most dangerous.

05 / Explore the detail

Payment Processing

Payment processors that work with forex often ask for a rolling reserve, holding back a share of deposits for a set period as protection against chargebacks. Some also want an upfront security deposit.

That means part of your clients’ deposits won’t reach your operating account straight away. Plan your cash flow around it.

06 / Explore the detail

Team and Operations

Even a lean brokerage needs people. At minimum, you’ll usually need:

A compliance officer, often a regulatory requirement

Someone to manage the dealing desk and risk

Customer support covering trading hours

Back office staff for payments and account queries

Sales or account managers, if you’re working with direct clients

Some of this can be outsourced at first, but salaries and contractor fees add up quickly. Budget at least a year of running costs here.

07 / Explore the detail

Marketing: The Cost People Underestimate

You can have a perfect setup and no clients. Marketing in forex is competitive and expensive, and many ad platforms restrict financial services advertising, which pushes costs up further.

Common channels include IB and affiliate partnerships, content marketing and SEO, paid ads where permitted, events and expos, and social media. IB programmes are often the most cost-effective at the start, because you pay mainly on results.

Whatever channels you choose, give marketing a real budget. Brokers who pour everything into setup and leave nothing for growth rarely get past their first year.

08 / Explore the detail

Putting a Budget Together

Rather than chasing one magic number, build your budget in layers:

Regulatory capital: the amount your chosen jurisdiction requires you to hold

Setup costs: licensing, legal, grey label setup, integrations, website

Twelve months of running costs: platform fees, tech subscriptions, staff, office, compliance

Liquidity and risk buffer: deposits for liquidity providers, plus a cushion for B-book exposure

Marketing: a realistic first-year budget for bringing in clients

Contingency: an extra margin for delays and surprises, because there will be some

Add those together and you have a figure grounded in your actual plans rather than a guess.

09 / Explore the detail

Ways to Keep Initial Capital Lower

If the total looks daunting, there are sensible ways to reduce it:

Start in a jurisdiction with lower capital requirements and expand later

Launch with a smaller set of instruments and account types

Choose a provider that bundles the server, CRM and bridge

Rely on IB partnerships instead of heavy paid marketing at first

Outsource compliance, support or dealing until volume justifies hiring

What you shouldn’t cut is your risk buffer or your runway. Those are what keep you alive while you build.

10 / Explore the detail

Conclusion

Your forex broker startup capital depends mostly on regulation, execution model and growth plans. The grey label is an important piece, but usually not the heaviest. Build your metatrader grey label budget around a full year of operations, keep a healthy buffer, and you’ll give your brokerage a real chance to grow.

If you’d like help estimating the platform side of your budget, MetaGreyLabel can give you a clear breakdown based on your markets and launch plans.

The context

For a lot of brokerages, partners bring in more clients than any ad campaign ever will. Introducing brokers, affiliates, signal providers and trading educators all have audiences that already trust them. When they recommend you, people listen.

But partners only stay loyal if you treat them well. That means accurate tracking, clear reports and commissions paid on time without arguments. A proper forex IB portal makes all of that automatic, so your partner programme can grow without turning into a spreadsheet nightmare.

01 / Explore the detail

Why Your Brokerage Needs Proper IB Tools

Plenty of brokers start by tracking partners manually. It works for a handful of IBs. Then the numbers grow, commission structures get more complicated, and mistakes start creeping in.

01

The Problems With Manual Tracking

Clients get assigned to the wrong partner. Commissions are calculated late or incorrectly. Partners can’t see their own numbers, so they email your team constantly. Disputes eat up time and damage relationships. And the best IBs quietly move to brokers who make their lives easier.

02

What Good Software Fixes

Automated tracking, transparent reporting and accurate commission calculations remove most of that friction. Your partners trust the numbers, your team stops firefighting, and your network grows faster.

02 / Explore the detail

What a Forex IB Portal Gives Your Partners

The IB portal is your partners’ own space, separate from the client trader’s room, where they manage everything about their relationship with you.

01

Unique Referral Links

Each partner gets their own tracking links and codes, so every client they bring in is assigned to them correctly from the moment of registration.

02

Live Performance Data

Partners can see how many clients they’ve referred, how many have funded accounts, and how much those clients are trading.

03

Commission Reports

Clear breakdowns of what they’ve earned, how it was calculated and when it will be paid. No guesswork and no need to email your team.

04

Marketing Materials

Banners, landing pages and promotional content they can use straight away, all carrying your branding.

05

Payout Requests

Partners can request commission withdrawals directly in the portal and track their status.

06

Multi-Level Visibility

If you run a tiered structure, master IBs can see the performance of their sub-IBs too.

03 / Explore the detail

Introducing Broker Software for Your Team

Good introducing broker software isn’t just about the partner-facing side. Your back office needs proper tools to manage the programme.

01

Partner Onboarding and Approval

Review IB applications, verify partner details and approve them through a clear workflow.

02

Client Assignment

Assign clients to partners automatically through referral links, or manually when needed. Move clients between partners with a full record of the change.

03

Flexible Commission Plans

Create different plans for different partners. A new affiliate might get a standard rate, while a high-volume IB gets a custom deal.

04

Fraud and Abuse Checks

Flag suspicious activity like self-referrals, duplicate accounts or unusual trading patterns designed to inflate commissions.

05

Detailed Reporting

See which partners bring in the most funded clients, the most volume and the best long-term value. Use that data to decide where to invest.

04 / Explore the detail

Forex Affiliate Management Made Simpler

Forex affiliate management has its own quirks. Affiliates often care about sign-ups and first deposits more than ongoing trading volume, so they may need a different setup from traditional IBs.

01

CPA Deals

Pay a fixed amount per qualified client, based on rules you set, such as minimum deposit or minimum trading activity.

02

Revenue Share

Pay a percentage of the revenue generated by referred clients over time.

03

Hybrid Deals

Combine an upfront CPA payment with an ongoing revenue share, which suits many larger affiliates.

04

Campaign Tracking

Track which campaigns, landing pages or channels bring in the best clients, so affiliates can focus their efforts and you can reward what works.

05 / Explore the detail

How the IB Commission System Works

The IB commission system is the engine behind your whole partner programme. When it’s accurate and transparent, partners trust you. When it isn’t, nothing else matters much.

01

Commission Types

Pay per lot traded, a share of spread, a share of commission, a fixed amount per trade, or a combination. Rates can vary by symbol, account type or partner.

02

Multi-Tier Structures

Reward master IBs for clients brought in by their sub-IBs, with clear rules on how commissions are split between levels.

03

Automatic Calculation

Commissions are calculated from real trading data synced from MetaTrader. No manual entry and no spreadsheets.

04

Scheduled Payouts

Pay commissions daily, weekly or monthly, either automatically or after approval. Payouts can go to a trading account or through your payment methods.

06 / Explore the detail

Built Into Your Brokerage Setup

With our grey label and turnkey packages, the IB and affiliate module connects directly to your CRM, trader’s room and MetaTrader server. Client assignments, trading data and commissions flow between them automatically, and we test everything before launch.

If you already use a separate IB system, we can connect it to your setup instead.

07 / Explore the detail

Turn Your Partners Into Your Strongest Growth Channel

A strong partner programme can bring in clients faster and more cheaply than most marketing. The right forex IB portal keeps your partners informed, paid accurately and motivated to keep referring.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I set different commission rates for different partners?

Yes. You can create separate plans for different partners, account types or symbols, and set custom deals for your top IBs.

Does the system support multi-level IB structures?

Yes. Master IBs can earn from sub-IBs below them, with clear rules for how commissions are split at each level.

Can partners see their reports in real time?

Yes. Partners can log in to their portal at any time to see referred clients, trading volumes and commission earnings.

How are commissions paid?

You choose the payout schedule and method. Commissions can be credited to a trading account or paid out through your connected payment options.

Brokerage insights

Introducing Broker (IB) Programs for MetaTrader Grey Label Businesses

Practical perspectives on brokerage technology and operations.

5 min read · Meta Grey Label

The context

Ask any established broker where their best clients came from, and there’s a good chance the answer is a person, not an ad. A trading educator with a loyal following. A local partner who runs workshops. A money manager who brought their investors along. That’s the introducing broker model, and for many brokerages it does more for growth than any paid campaign.

If you run a MetaTrader grey label, you’re in a good position to build a strong forex ib program, because you control the server, the account groups and the data that make IB rewards work. Here’s how to do it well.

01 / Explore the detail

What an IB Actually Does

An introducing broker refers clients to your brokerage in exchange for a share of the revenue those clients generate. They don’t hold client funds or execute trades. That stays with you. Their job is to find traders, build trust and point them your way.

IBs come in many shapes:

Trading educators and course creators

Signal providers and analysts

Local agents who handle relationships in a specific country

Affiliates who run websites, YouTube channels or social accounts

Money managers bringing their investor base

Each brings a different kind of client, and each tends to want a slightly different deal.

02 / Explore the detail

Why Grey Label Makes IB Programmes Easier to Run

On a white label, your IB options are often limited by how the host sets up groups and reporting. With a grey label, you have admin access to your own server, so you can design your programme around your business instead of someone else’s setup.

A well-built metatrader grey label ib structure lets you:

Create dedicated account groups for each IB, with their own spreads or commissions

Track every trade back to the IB who referred the client

Pull accurate volume and revenue data straight from your own server

Adjust conditions for top-performing partners without affecting other clients

That flexibility matters. Good IBs compare brokers carefully, and the ability to offer tailored terms is often what wins them over.

03 / Explore the detail

Common IB Reward Structures

There’s no single right way to pay IBs. Most brokers use one of these models, or a mix.

01

Rebates per Lot

The IB earns a fixed amount for every lot their clients trade. It’s simple and transparent, and it’s popular with IBs whose clients trade actively.

02

Spread Markups

The IB’s clients trade on slightly wider spreads, and the IB keeps the difference. This gives the IB some control over their earnings, but it needs careful handling so clients still get competitive pricing.

03

Revenue Share

The IB receives a percentage of the net revenue their clients generate. This lines up the IB’s interests with yours, but it requires clear, trustworthy reporting, because IBs will want to see exactly how revenue is worked out.

04

CPA (Cost per Acquisition)

A one-off payment for each client who meets set conditions, such as a minimum deposit and trading volume. This is more common with affiliates than traditional IBs, and it needs strong fraud controls.

05

Multi-Level Structures

IBs can recruit sub-IBs and earn a share of their commissions. This can grow your network quickly, but it gets complicated fast. Keep the number of levels manageable and the rules very clear.

04 / Explore the detail

The Tools You Need

Running an IB programme on spreadsheets works for about three partners. After that, it becomes a source of errors and arguments.

At minimum, you’ll want:

An IB module in your CRM that tracks referrals, works out commissions and handles multiple levels

Real-time sync with your MetaTrader server so trade data feeds into commission calculations automatically

An IB portal where partners can see their clients, volumes and earnings without emailing your team

Tracking links and promo materials that make it easy for IBs to send traffic your way

Automated payouts on a fixed schedule

The IB portal especially is worth getting right. Partners who can see their numbers clearly trust you more and complain less.

05 / Explore the detail

Pay Accurately, Pay on Time

This sounds obvious, but it’s where many IB programmes fall apart. IBs talk to each other. A broker who pays late or gets calculations wrong will hear about it, and so will every other IB in that network.

Set a clear payout schedule and stick to it. Make sure commission calculations match what IBs see in their portal. If a mistake happens, fix it fast and explain what went wrong. Your reputation with partners is worth far more than the cost of a correction.

06 / Explore the detail

Protect Yourself From Abuse

Most IBs are honest, but any reward system attracts a few people looking to game it. Common problems include:

IBs trading heavily on their own linked accounts just to generate rebates

Clients and IBs coordinating trades that cancel each other out across accounts

Fake or duplicate accounts set up to trigger CPA payments

Churning, where clients are pushed to overtrade to boost commissions

With a grey label, you can watch for these patterns directly on your server. Risk tools that flag linked accounts and unusual trading behaviour are worth having before your programme grows. Clear terms that allow you to hold or cancel payouts for abuse help too.

07 / Explore the detail

Treat IBs as Partners, Not Lead Sources

The brokers with the strongest IB networks don’t just send a contract and a tracking link. They invest in the relationship.

That might mean a dedicated account manager for top partners, co-branded webinars or materials, early access to new account types or features, or regular calls to hear what their clients are asking for. IBs are close to the market. They often know what traders want before your marketing team does.

08 / Explore the detail

Getting Started

If you’re building a programme from scratch, keep the first version simple:

One or two reward structures you can explain in a sentence

A clean IB portal with accurate, real-time data

A fixed monthly or weekly payout schedule

Clear terms covering abuse and payout conditions

Add complexity only once the basics run smoothly and you understand which partners are actually bringing in quality clients.

09 / Explore the detail

Conclusion

A strong forex ib program can become your most dependable growth channel, as long as it’s built on accurate data, fair rewards and on-time payouts. Running a metatrader grey label ib setup gives you the control to design the programme your partners actually want, rather than whatever a host allows.

If you’re planning to launch or improve an IB programme, MetaGreyLabel can help you set up the groups, tracking and integrations to support it.

The context

Every new client has to be checked before they trade. That’s not optional, and for good reason. But the way it’s done can make a huge difference. A slow, confusing verification process loses clients before they ever deposit. A sloppy one leaves your brokerage exposed to fraud, money laundering and trouble with regulators.

Good forex KYC software gets the balance right. Clients move through verification quickly. Your compliance team gets the information and records it needs. And your brokerage stays on the right side of the rules in the markets you serve.

01 / Explore the detail

Why KYC Matters So Much for Brokers

KYC, or Know Your Customer, is the process of confirming who your clients are and assessing the risk they might bring. For brokers, it’s closely tied to anti-money laundering rules and regulatory requirements.

01

Protecting Your Licence

Regulators expect brokers to verify clients properly and keep records. Weak KYC can lead to fines, restrictions or worse.

02

Protecting Your Business

Fraudulent accounts, stolen identities and payment chargebacks cost money and damage your relationships with payment providers and banks.

03

Protecting Your Clients

Proper checks help keep criminals off your platform and show genuine clients that you take security seriously.

02 / Explore the detail

Forex Client Onboarding That Doesn’t Lose People

Smooth forex client onboarding is where good compliance and good business meet. The goal is to collect what you need without making clients feel like they’re filling in a tax return.

01

Simple Registration

Clients start with basic details, confirm their email and get access to the trader’s room straight away. Verification steps follow inside the portal.

02

Clear Document Upload

Clients upload ID and proof of address directly from their phone or computer. The portal shows exactly what’s needed and why, which cuts down on wrong or incomplete submissions.

03

Visible Progress

Clients can see where they are in the process, what’s been approved and what’s still missing. Fewer “where’s my account?” emails for your support team.

04

Suitability and Appropriateness Questions

Where your regulator requires it, clients answer questions about trading experience, financial knowledge and risk understanding. Answers are stored with their profile.

05

Faster Approvals

With the right integrations, many checks can happen automatically, so lower-risk clients get approved quickly while higher-risk ones are flagged for review.

03 / Explore the detail

Forex Compliance Tools for Your Team

Behind the client-facing steps, your compliance team needs proper forex compliance tools to review, decide and record.

01

Document Review Queue

All pending verifications appear in one queue. Staff can view documents, compare them against client details and approve, reject or request more information.

02

Risk Scoring

Assign risk levels based on factors like country, deposit size, source of funds or profile information. Higher-risk clients can be routed for enhanced checks.

03

Ongoing Monitoring

KYC isn’t a one-time job. Track document expiry dates, flag profile changes and highlight unusual deposit or withdrawal patterns for review.

04

Restrictions by Country

Block or limit registrations from jurisdictions you don’t serve or can’t accept clients from under your licence.

05

Full Audit Trail

Every document, decision and status change is recorded with a timestamp and the name of the staff member involved. Ready when auditors or regulators ask.

06

Compliance Reporting

See verification rates, pending reviews, rejected applications, expiring documents and risk levels across your client base.

04 / Explore the detail

Broker KYC Integration With Verification Providers

Manual document checks work at small volumes. As your brokerage grows, broker KYC integration with specialist verification providers can save a lot of time.

01

Automated ID Verification

Connect services that check identity documents for authenticity and match them against the client’s details.

02

Liveness and Selfie Checks

Confirm that the person registering is real and matches their ID, which helps stop identity fraud.

03

Sanctions and PEP Screening

Screen clients against sanctions lists and politically exposed persons databases as part of your AML checks.

04

Address Verification

Verify proof of address documents automatically where supported.

05

Use the Providers You Prefer

If you already work with a verification provider, we can connect it. If not, we can talk through options that suit your markets and volumes.

05 / Explore the detail

Built Into Your Brokerage Setup

With our grey label and turnkey packages, the KYC and compliance module is part of your CRM, trader’s room and back office. Client data flows through the whole system, so verification status controls what clients can do, such as depositing or trading, without manual intervention.

01

Configured for Your Licence

Requirements differ by jurisdiction. We set up document types, questions, approval workflows and restrictions to match what you’ve been told you need. Your legal or compliance advisor should confirm the exact requirements for your licence.

02

Tested Before Launch

We run through every onboarding scenario, from a clean approval to a rejected document to a high-risk flag, so your team knows exactly how the process works.

Whether you need dependable forex KYC software, smoother forex client onboarding, practical forex compliance tools for your team, or broker KYC integration with verification providers, we’ll help you build a process that works. Get in touch today.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I customise the documents and questions clients see?

Yes. We configure the required documents, onboarding questions and approval steps to match your licence and target markets.

Can verification be automated?

Partly, yes. By integrating third-party verification providers, many ID, liveness and screening checks can run automatically, with your team reviewing only flagged cases.

Can I stop unverified clients from depositing or trading?

Yes. You can set rules so clients must reach a certain verification level before they can fund their account, trade or withdraw.

Does the system keep records for regulators?

Yes. Documents, decisions and changes are stored with a full audit trail, ready for internal reviews or regulatory requests.

07 / Explore the detail

Make Compliance a Strength, Not a Bottleneck

Strong verification protects your licence, your partners and your clients. Done well, it also helps genuine traders get started faster.

The context

Most traders will never hear the word “bridge.” They’ll just notice whether their orders fill quickly and at the price they expected. Behind every one of those fills is a piece of technology doing a lot of work in a fraction of a second.

A forex liquidity bridge is what connects your MetaTrader platform to the outside market. Get it right and execution feels effortless. Get it wrong and you’ll hear about it from your clients, usually during the busiest moments of the trading day. We set up, configure and support bridges so your brokerage runs smoothly from the first trade.

01 / Operational scope

What a Liquidity Bridge Actually Does

MetaTrader on its own doesn’t connect directly to most liquidity providers. It needs something in between that speaks both languages. That’s the bridge.

01

Bringing Prices In

The bridge receives price feeds from your liquidity providers and passes them into MetaTrader, so your clients see live, tradable quotes.

02

Sending Orders Out

When a client places a trade that should go to the market, the bridge sends it to your provider, receives the confirmation and updates the client’s position in MetaTrader.

03

Applying Your Rules

The bridge also applies your routing logic. Which trades go out, which stay in-house, which provider gets each order and how markups are applied. It’s where your execution model actually lives.

02 / Operational scope

MT4 Bridge and MT5 Bridge Options

Whichever platform you run, we can connect it properly. Many brokers run both, and the bridge handles each one.

01

MT4 Bridge

An MT4 bridge connects your MT4 server to liquidity providers through server-side plugins. It’s a mature setup, widely used, and well suited to forex-focused brokerages with traders who rely on MT4.

02

MT5 Bridge

An MT5 bridge typically connects through MT5’s gateway architecture, which was designed with external connectivity in mind. It handles multi-asset liquidity well, making it a strong choice if you offer indices, metals, energies, stocks or crypto CFDs.

03

Running Both Through One Bridge

If you operate MT4 and MT5 together, a single bridge setup can serve both platforms. That keeps your routing rules, provider connections and reporting consistent across your whole brokerage.

03 / Operational scope

Key Features to Look For

Not every bridge is equal. When we set one up, these are the areas we pay most attention to.

01

Low Latency

Every millisecond matters, especially during fast markets. We host and configure bridges to keep the path between your server and providers as short as possible.

02

Liquidity Aggregation

Connect several providers and combine their prices into one feed. The bridge picks the best available quote, which can tighten spreads and improve fills.

03

Flexible Routing Rules

Route flow by client, group, symbol, trade size or exposure level. This is what makes A book, B book and hybrid models workable in practice.

04

Failover Protection

If one provider goes offline or starts quoting badly, the bridge can switch to another automatically. Your clients keep trading while you deal with the issue.

05

Markup and Commission Control

Apply spread markups and commissions by group or symbol directly in the bridge, so your pricing strategy is easy to manage and adjust.

06

Clear Reporting

Execution reports, fill statistics, slippage data and provider performance help your dealing team spot problems early and keep improving.

04 / Operational scope

Why the Bridge for Forex Brokers Deserves Attention

Choosing a bridge for forex brokers is often treated as an afterthought, squeezed in after the platform and CRM are picked. That’s a mistake.

A poorly configured bridge can cause requotes, rejected orders, frozen prices and slippage complaints. It can leave your dealing team blind to exposure. And it can turn a liquidity provider outage into a full brokerage outage. Getting this part right protects both your clients and your reputation.

05 / Operational scope

How We Set Up Your Bridge

01

Understand Your Execution Model

We start with how you plan to run your book. A book, B book or hybrid. Which providers you’re using. Which instruments you’ll offer. That shapes how the bridge is built.

02

Connect Your Providers

We set up connections to your chosen liquidity providers, or help you choose providers if you’re starting fresh.

03

Configure Routing and Pricing

Routing rules, aggregation logic, markups and failover settings are configured around your business model.

04

Test Under Real Conditions

We test fills, latency, failover and reporting before launch, including what happens when a provider drops out.

05

Monitor and Support

Once live, we keep an eye on performance and help your team adjust settings as your client flow changes.

06 / Operational scope

Part of Your Grey Label or Turnkey Setup

If you’re launching with one of our grey label or turnkey packages, the bridge is set up as part of your brokerage. If you run your own admin licence, we can install and manage a bridge on your server, or improve one you already have.

07 / Operational scope

Build Execution Your Clients Can Rely On

Your clients trust you with every order they place. A well-built forex liquidity bridge is how you keep that trust, trade after trade.

Whether you need an MT4 bridge, an MT5 bridge or a single bridge for forex brokers running both platforms, we’ll help you set it up properly and keep it running smoothly. Get in touch today.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need a liquidity bridge if I run a B book?

Even B book brokers usually need a bridge. It lets you hedge large or risky positions and gives you the routing tools to move to a hybrid model when needed.

Can I connect more than one liquidity provider?

Yes. A bridge can connect several providers, aggregate their pricing and switch between them automatically if one has problems.

Will changing liquidity providers mean rebuilding my bridge?

No. Providers can be added, removed or swapped within your bridge setup without disrupting your MetaTrader server or clients.

How long does bridge setup take?

For standard setups, connection and configuration can be completed within a few days, once your provider accounts are active. Complex routing rules or multiple providers may take a little longer.

MetaTrader Grey Label + CRM Integration: Boosting Client Onboarding and Retention

Practical perspectives on brokerage technology and operations.

5 min read · Meta Grey Label

The context

Here’s something brokers often find out too late. You can have excellent execution, tight spreads and a well-run server, and still lose clients before they place a single trade. They sign up, hit a clunky KYC form, wait two days for an account, struggle to deposit, and quietly give up.

Most of that friction has nothing to do with MetaTrader itself. It happens in the space between your website, your back office and your trading server. That’s what a proper forex crm integration is meant to fix.

01 / Explore the detail

What the CRM Actually Does in a Brokerage

In a forex brokerage, the CRM is far more than a contact list. It’s the system that handles almost everything a client does outside the trading terminal:

Registration and identity verification

Creating live and demo accounts

Deposits, withdrawals and internal transfers

Support tickets and communication

IB and affiliate tracking

Sales pipelines and lead management

Your clients see the client portal. Your team sees the back office. Underneath, the CRM keeps both connected to your MetaTrader server.

02 / Explore the detail

Why Integration Matters More on a Grey Label

With a white label, you’re often stuck with whatever CRM the host supports, connected however they’ve decided to connect it. With a grey label, you run your own server with admin access, so you can integrate the CRM properly and decide how data flows between the two.

A well-built metatrader grey label crm connection means accounts get created automatically, balances update in real time, group changes happen without anyone typing them in, and your team can see a client’s full picture in one place. Done badly, you end up with staff copying numbers between systems and clients asking why their deposit hasn’t shown up.

03 / Explore the detail

How Integration Improves Onboarding

The first few days of a client’s relationship with you matter enormously. Most drop-off happens right here.

01

Faster Account Opening

When your CRM is linked directly to your MetaTrader server, a client can register, pass verification and receive login details within minutes. No manual step where someone in your back office creates the account by hand and emails credentials the next morning.

That speed matters. A trader who signs up while excited about a setup they’ve spotted wants to trade now, not tomorrow.

02

Smoother KYC

Good CRMs let clients upload documents straight from their phone, run automatic ID checks where your regulator allows it, and flag only the cases that really need a human to review. Your compliance team spends its time on the tricky files instead of approving obvious ones.

03

Deposits That Just Work

Payment gateways connect through the CRM. When everything is integrated, a deposit made through the portal lands in the client’s MetaTrader balance automatically. No waiting, no support ticket asking where the money went.

This is often the single biggest factor in whether a new client goes on to trade. Make the first deposit easy and most of the battle is won.

04 / Explore the detail

How Integration Improves Retention

Getting a client through the door is only half the job. Keeping them is where long-term revenue comes from.

01

A Full View of Every Client

With your CRM pulling trading data from MetaTrader, your team can see not just who a client is, but how they trade. Deposit history, trading frequency, favourite instruments, open positions, recent losses.

That context changes how you support people. A client who has gone quiet for two weeks after a run of losing trades needs a different conversation from one who just made their third deposit in a month.

02

Automated, Relevant Communication

Integration lets you trigger messages based on real behaviour. A welcome sequence for new accounts. A reminder for clients who registered but never funded. A note about a new account type for traders who’d clearly benefit from it.

The key word is relevant. Clients ignore generic newsletters but respond to messages that clearly fit their situation.

03

Quicker Withdrawals

Nothing hurts retention like slow withdrawals. When your CRM, payments and MetaTrader server are all connected, withdrawal requests can be checked, approved and processed far faster. Fast, reliable payouts build the kind of trust that keeps clients around and gets them recommending you.

04

Support That Knows the Context

When a client contacts support, your agent should be able to see their account, recent trades and payment history straight away. No asking for login numbers, no transferring between departments. Small thing, big difference in how people feel about your brokerage.

05 / Explore the detail

The IB Side of the Equation

If introducing brokers are part of your growth plan, integration matters even more. Your CRM needs accurate trade data from MetaTrader to calculate rebates correctly. When the two are properly linked, commissions are worked out automatically and IBs can follow their earnings in their own portal.

Get it wrong and you’ll spend hours fixing disputes. IBs talk to each other, and a reputation for unreliable payouts spreads fast.

06 / Explore the detail

What to Look for in a CRM Integration

Not every CRM connects equally well. When assessing options, ask:

Does it support your MetaTrader version and work with grey label servers?

Is the connection real time, or does data sync in batches?

Can it handle several servers, such as separate live and demo environments?

How does it deal with errors, like a failed deposit or a duplicate account?

Is the client portal mobile-friendly and easy to brand?

Can it grow with you as you add copy trading, PAMM or more payment methods?

Ask for a demo using a test MetaTrader server, not just slides. Watching an account being created, funded and traded end to end tells you more than any feature list.

07 / Explore the detail

Common Mistakes to Avoid

A few things trip brokers up regularly:

Launching before payment gateways are properly tested through the CRM

Mismatched group names between the CRM and MetaTrader, causing accounts to land in the wrong group

Too many manual approval steps that slow onboarding for no real compliance reason

Not training support staff on the back office before going live

Each is easy to fix early and painful to fix later.

08 / Explore the detail

Conclusion

Your trading platform gets clients to trade. Your CRM gets them to sign up, fund and stay. A solid forex crm integration ties the two together so clients have a smooth experience from registration to withdrawal, and your team spends less time fixing data and more time helping people.

If you’re setting up or improving your metatrader grey label crm connection, MetaGreyLabel can help you plan an integration that suits your onboarding flow and growth targets.
