The context

Every broker wants the deep, tight pricing that big banks offer. Very few can get it directly. Tier 1 banks typically ask for large capital deposits, strong credit history and trading volumes most new and mid-sized brokers simply don’t have yet.

That’s where prime of prime forex liquidity comes in. A prime of prime provider sits between you and the top-tier banks, giving you access to institutional-grade pricing on terms a growing brokerage can actually meet. This page explains how it works, what to look for and how we help you connect.

01 / Explore the detail

What Is Prime of Prime?

To understand prime of prime, it helps to start with prime brokerage.

01

Prime Brokers

Large banks offer prime brokerage services to big institutions, hedge funds and major trading firms. Those clients get direct access to bank liquidity, credit lines and settlement services. The entry requirements are high.

02

Prime of Prime Providers

A prime of prime provider holds a relationship with one or more prime brokers. It then extends that access to smaller firms, like retail brokers, who wouldn’t qualify on their own. In effect, it takes institutional liquidity and repackages it for businesses that need lower minimums and simpler onboarding.

03

Why It Exists

The gap between what big banks offer and what smaller brokers need is huge. Prime of prime fills that gap. It’s now the most common route to quality liquidity for retail-focused brokerages.

02 / Explore the detail

What a PoP Liquidity Provider Offers

A good PoP liquidity provider gives you much more than a price feed.

01

Aggregated Pricing

Most PoP providers pull prices from several tier 1 banks and non-bank market makers. That aggregation can produce tighter spreads and deeper liquidity than any single source.

02

Lower Entry Requirements

Minimum deposits, credit requirements and volume commitments are usually far lower than going direct to a bank. That makes institutional-quality pricing achievable much earlier in your brokerage’s life.

03

Multi-Asset Access

Many PoP providers offer forex alongside metals, energies, indices, stocks and crypto CFDs, which suits brokers running MT5 or planning to expand their product range.

04

Credit and Settlement

The provider handles the credit relationship with prime brokers and the complex settlement processes behind it, so your team doesn’t have to.

03 / Explore the detail

Prime of Prime for Small Brokers: Why It Makes Sense

For most new and mid-sized brokerages, prime of prime for small brokers isn’t a compromise. It’s the sensible choice.

01

Start Without Huge Capital

You can access quality pricing without tying up large amounts of money in bank deposits. That capital can go into marketing, compliance and growing your team instead.

02

Compete on Pricing

Better liquidity means tighter spreads and more reliable fills, which helps you compete with larger, more established brokers for the same traders.

03

Grow Into Bigger Relationships

As your volumes rise, you may negotiate better terms with your PoP provider, add more providers, or eventually approach banks directly. Prime of prime gives you a solid base to build from.

04 / Explore the detail

How to Choose a Prime of Prime Provider

Not every provider labelled prime of prime offers the same quality. These are the questions worth asking.

01

Where Does the Liquidity Come From?

Ask how many sources they aggregate and what kind of institutions those sources are. Vague answers are a warning sign.

02

What Are Their Execution Statistics?

Fill rates, average latency, slippage data and rejection rates tell you far more than marketing claims about tight spreads.

03

Are They Regulated?

Check where the provider is regulated and how client funds are protected. Your own regulator may have expectations here too.

04

What Are the Real Costs?

Look beyond headline spreads. Ask about commissions, minimum volumes, monthly fees and any charges for connectivity or data.

05

How Do They Connect to MetaTrader?

Make sure they work smoothly with your bridge and platform setup, whether you’re on MT4, MT5 or both.

06

What Is Their Support Like?

When something goes wrong during a busy session, you need someone who responds fast. Ask how support works and how quickly they act on issues.

05 / Explore the detail

How We Help You Work With Prime of Prime Providers

We don’t sell liquidity ourselves. Our job is to help you connect to the right providers and make sure the technology between them and your platform works properly.

01

Guidance on Choosing Providers

We’ll help you think through which providers suit your client profile, volumes and target markets, and what to ask during your discussions with them.

02

Bridge and Integration

We connect your chosen PoP providers to your MetaTrader server through a properly configured liquidity bridge, with routing, aggregation and failover set up around your business model.

03

Multiple Providers

Many brokers connect two or more providers for better pricing and backup. We handle the aggregation so it all reaches your clients as one clean feed.

04

Ongoing Monitoring

Once you’re live, we help your team track execution quality and spot problems before clients notice them.

06 / Explore the detail

Get Institutional Pricing on Realistic Terms

You don’t need to be a giant to offer your clients strong pricing and reliable execution. Prime of prime forex liquidity gives growing brokers access to the kind of depth that was once reserved for major institutions.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

Is prime of prime liquidity as good as direct bank liquidity?

For most retail brokers, a good PoP provider offers pricing close to what they could get directly, with far lower barriers. Very large brokers may eventually benefit from direct relationships, but that’s usually much further down the line.

What deposit does a prime of prime provider usually require?

It varies by provider, asset classes and expected volumes. Requirements are generally much lower than going direct to a tier 1 bank. Ask each provider for their specific terms.

Can I use more than one PoP provider?

Yes, and many brokers do. Connecting several providers through your bridge can improve pricing and gives you backup if one source has issues.

Can I connect a prime of prime provider to my grey label?

Yes. Liquidity connection is part of our grey label and turnkey setups, and we can connect the PoP providers you choose.

Brokerage insights

Revenue Streams of a MetaTrader Grey Label Brokerage: Spreads, Commissions and More

Practical perspectives on brokerage technology and operations.

6 min read · Meta Grey Label

The context

New brokers often build their business plan around one idea: clients trade, we take a small cut, repeat. It’s a reasonable starting point, but it misses most of what separates a brokerage that scrapes by from one that does well. The money comes in through several doors, and each one behaves differently when markets go quiet, when a big client leaves, or when a regulator changes the rules.

Running a grey label puts the controls for most of those doors in your hands. So it pays to know exactly what each one is and how to set it.

01 / Explore the detail

Why Control Over Pricing Changes Everything

On a white label, a lot of your pricing is shaped by the host. You might be able to tweak spreads within a range, but execution, swaps and group settings often come pre-set.

A grey label is different. With admin access to your own MetaTrader server, you decide what clients pay and how their trades are handled. That’s what makes it possible to design a revenue model around your actual clients instead of someone else’s defaults. It’s also why forex broker revenue on a grey label can look quite different from one brokerage to the next, even when they use similar technology.

02 / Explore the detail

The Markup on Every Price

Your liquidity provider streams you prices. You show clients slightly different ones. The gap between them is your markup, and it’s the most familiar source of income in the industry.

What many brokers overlook is how precisely this can be tuned. Rather than adding the same markup everywhere, you can:

Keep majors like EURUSD and GBPUSD sharp, since traders compare them constantly

Price exotics and less liquid instruments more generously, where clients expect wider spreads

Set different markups for beginner accounts, VIP accounts and IB-referred groups

A small change across a busy symbol adds up quickly. Equally, getting greedy on the pairs everyone watches is the fastest way to lose experienced traders.

03 / Explore the detail

Charging Per Trade Instead

Not every trader wants costs hidden in the spread. Scalpers, algorithmic traders and high-volume clients usually prefer raw pricing and a visible commission per lot. They can calculate exactly what each trade costs, which matters a great deal for their strategies.

Offering a commission-based account can bring in clients who would never consider a standard account. On your grey label server, you can set commissions by group, scale them down for higher volumes, or create special terms for professional clients and money managers.

01

Picking the Right Mix

Most brokers offer both. A standard account with no commission and slightly wider spreads works for newer or occasional traders. A raw account with commission suits the serious crowd. Running both lets you serve each group without forcing either into a model they dislike.

04 / Explore the detail

Overnight Positions

Clients who keep trades open past the daily rollover pay or earn swap, based on the interest rate gap between two currencies. Brokers add a margin on top of the base rate.

It’s quiet money, rarely noticed by short-term traders but steady across longer-term positions. Since you set swap rates yourself on a grey label, you can stay competitive on popular pairs while earning a fair amount elsewhere.

If you offer swap-free accounts, plan them carefully. A fixed holding fee after a certain number of days is common, but the terms need to be transparent and applied consistently.

05 / Explore the detail

Taking the Other Side

This is the part of brokerage income people argue about most.

When you keep a client’s trade in-house rather than passing it to the market, you become the counterparty. Their loss is your gain, and their gain is your cost. This is known as B-booking.

Many brokers combine approaches. Large, consistently profitable or fast-trading clients go to liquidity providers. Smaller, less experienced flow stays internal. Handled with discipline, this hybrid approach can be a major contributor to metatrader grey label profit.

The word “discipline” is doing a lot of work there. Without proper risk tools, clear routing rules and someone watching exposure in real time, B-book revenue can turn negative very quickly. A grey label gives you the access to set all of this up yourself, but it doesn’t remove the risk.

06 / Explore the detail

Income From Copy Trading and Managed Money

Copy trading, PAMM and MAM accounts add another layer. You can earn a share of performance or subscription fees charged by strategy providers and money managers.

The bigger effect, though, is volume. A single trader with a few hundred followers turns one decision into hundreds of trades. Each of those carries spread, commission or swap revenue, which can make a well-run copy trading platform one of the more valuable parts of the business.

07 / Explore the detail

Smaller Streams That Still Count

Beyond trading, a few extras can help:

VPS hosting for clients running EAs around the clock

Paid education, mentoring or premium webinars

Signal services and advanced analytics tools

New instruments such as share CFDs, commodities or crypto, where permitted

Individually they’re modest. Together, they can noticeably improve your margins and make your offering feel more complete.

08 / Explore the detail

Fees: Use Sparingly

Inactivity fees, withdrawal charges and conversion fees can bring in some revenue, but they come at a cost to trust. Traders are quick to share stories of brokers who nickel-and-dime them. Many brokers now treat zero-fee deposits and withdrawals as part of their marketing and earn their money through trading instead. If you do charge anything, keep it modest and spell it out clearly.

09 / Explore the detail

Where the Money Goes Out

Revenue isn’t profit. Before you can judge whether your model works, account for what flows the other way:

Grey label, bridge, CRM and other technology fees

Liquidity and execution costs

Payment processor fees and rolling reserves

IB rebates and affiliate payouts

Salaries, compliance, audits and office costs

Marketing and acquisition spend

B-book losses during periods when clients do well

IB rebates often surprise new brokers. Generous payouts can absorb most of the spread revenue from referred clients, so set rebate levels with your margins in mind, not just to win partners.

10 / Explore the detail

Don’t Lean on One Stream

Brokerages that rely heavily on a single source of income are fragile. A regulator restricting leverage, a key IB leaving, or a long stretch of calm markets can hit hard.

The more resilient approach spreads income across markups, commissions, swaps, carefully managed internal flow, copy trading volume and a few value-added services. When one slows, the others keep the lights on.

11 / Explore the detail

Conclusion

Steady forex broker revenue doesn’t come from squeezing clients. It comes from pricing each product thoughtfully, managing risk properly and building several income sources that support each other. A grey label gives you direct access to every one of those levers, and that’s where real metatrader grey label profit starts.

If you’d like to talk through pricing, group structures or routing on your own server, MetaGreyLabel can help you set things up around your goals.

Brokerage insights

Step-by-Step Guide to Setting Up a MetaTrader Grey Label Brokerage in Under a Week

Practical perspectives on brokerage technology and operations.

6 min read · Meta Grey Label

The context

A week sounds ambitious, and in some cases it is. But brokers who show up prepared regularly go from signed agreement to live trading in five or six days. The ones who take a month usually aren’t held up by the technology. They’re held up by missing documents, undecided trading conditions, or a liquidity provider that hasn’t finished onboarding them.

So this guide covers two things: what happens during a MetaTrader grey label setup, and what you need sorted beforehand so the week actually stays a week.

01 / Explore the detail

Before Day One: What Has to Be Ready

This is the part people skip, and it’s the reason most timelines slip. A fast forex broker setup depends far more on your preparation than on your provider’s speed.

Before you sign anything, try to have these in place:

A registered company, plus a license or a clear regulatory route

A corporate bank account and at least one payment processor that will work with forex

A domain and a basic website, even a simple one

A rough idea of your target markets and client types

A liquidity provider you’ve spoken to, or are happy to take from your provider’s network

If you’re still waiting on any of these, the server can be ready long before your business is. That’s fine, but don’t count the week until these are close to done.

02 / Explore the detail

Step 1: Agree on Your Server Specs and Sign Off (Day 1)

Once you’ve chosen a provider, the first conversation is about the server itself. Which platform, MT5 or MT4 where it’s still available? Where should the server be hosted? Most brokers pick a data centre close to their liquidity, often London, New York or Singapore, to keep latency down.

You’ll also confirm what’s included: admin and manager terminals, backup servers, web and mobile terminals, and any plugins bundled in the package. Get this in writing. “I thought that was included” is a surprisingly common reason for delays on day four.

03 / Explore the detail

Step 2: Branding and Server Deployment (Days 1 to 2)

While the provider spins up your dedicated server, they’ll need your branding files. That usually means your company name as it should appear in the terminal, your logo in the formats they request, and the server name your clients will search for when they log in.

Choose the server name carefully. Clients will type it into a terminal, so keep it short and obvious. Something like YourBrand-Live and YourBrand-Demo works better than anything clever.

Deployment itself is often done within 24 to 48 hours. The work is mostly on the provider’s side, so this is a good time to get going on Step 3.

04 / Explore the detail

Step 3: Build Your Trading Conditions (Days 2 to 3)

This is where your input matters most, and where indecision costs the most time.

01

Symbols and Groups

Decide which instruments you’re offering at launch. Starting smaller is usually smarter: major and minor FX pairs, gold, maybe a handful of indices. You can add crypto CFDs or shares later.

Then set up your account groups. Most brokers launch with two or three account types, perhaps a standard account, a raw spread account with commission, and a demo group. Each group needs its own leverage, margin call and stop-out levels, swap settings and commission rules.

02

Execution Model

Will you send everything to liquidity (A-book), keep some flow in-house (B-book), or run a hybrid? This shapes how your bridge and risk tools get configured, so decide it now, not after launch. If you’re unsure, a hybrid model with clear routing rules is a common starting point, though it does need someone watching it.

05 / Explore the detail

Step 4: Connect Liquidity and the Bridge (Days 3 to 4)

With a grey label, you’re not locked into one liquidity source, which is a big part of why brokers choose it. Your provider connects your server to the liquidity provider through a bridge, then maps your symbols to theirs.

Expect a bit of back and forth here. Symbol naming, contract sizes and price precision all need to match. A small mismatch, like a gold contract set to 100 ounces on one side and 1 ounce on the other, can cause real trouble once live money is involved. Test every symbol, not just EURUSD.

06 / Explore the detail

Step 5: Plug In Your CRM, Payments and Client Area (Days 4 to 5)

Your traders won’t only see MetaTrader. They’ll see your client portal, where they register, upload KYC documents, deposit and withdraw. Most grey label providers either include a forex CRM or integrate one you already use.

On this step you’ll:

Connect the CRM to your MetaTrader server so accounts are created automatically

Add your payment gateways and test a few real deposits and withdrawals

Set up KYC rules that match what your regulator expects

Configure email notifications so they sound like your brand, not a template

Payments are often the slowest piece of the whole process, mostly because processors take their time approving forex merchants. If yours isn’t live yet, launch with bank wire and add cards later.

07 / Explore the detail

Step 6: Test Everything, Then Test It Again (Days 5 to 6)

Open a few live accounts with small amounts. Place trades on different symbols. Check that swaps calculate correctly overnight. Trigger a margin call on purpose. Make a withdrawal and time how long it takes.

Have someone who wasn’t involved in the setup try to break it. They’ll find the awkward spots your team has stopped noticing.

01

A Quick Pre-Launch Checklist

Admin and manager terminals working for your team

Backup server tested

Reports exporting properly for your back office and regulator

Risk alerts going to the right people

Support team trained on how the platform works and how to answer common client questions

08 / Explore the detail

Step 7: Go Live (Day 6 or 7)

Launch quietly. Bring in a small group of clients first, maybe from an IB you trust or your own network, and watch how the system handles real activity for a few days before you put money into marketing.

That soft launch is your safety net. Anything you missed in testing will show up here, while volumes are still small enough to fix calmly.

09 / Explore the detail

What Usually Slows Things Down

To be honest, it’s rarely the server. A MetaTrader grey label setup on the technical side can be finished in a few days by an experienced provider. Delays tend to come from:

Trading conditions that keep changing after configuration has started

Liquidity providers with slow onboarding

Payment processors still reviewing your application

Missing branding files or late sign-offs

Sort those out early and a one-week launch is realistic.

10 / Explore the detail

Conclusion

A fast forex broker setup comes down to preparation, quick decisions and a provider who has done this many times before. Get your business groundwork in order, know your trading conditions before day one, and leave enough time for proper testing.

If you’re planning your launch, MetaGreyLabel can take you through a timeline built around your markets, your liquidity and your launch date.

Brokerage insights

Trader’s Room and Client Portal Features in a MetaTrader Grey Label Setup

Practical perspectives on brokerage technology and operations.

6 min read · Meta Grey Label

The context

Your traders spend most of their time in MetaTrader. But almost everything else they do with your brokerage happens somewhere else: signing up, verifying their identity, funding an account, moving money between accounts, asking for help, withdrawing profits. All of that happens in the client portal, often called the trader’s room.

It’s easy to treat the portal as an afterthought, something you sort out once the server is running. That’s a mistake. For many clients, the portal is your brokerage. It’s the first thing they use and the place they come back to every time money is involved.

Here’s what a strong forex client portal should include, and how it fits into a grey label setup.

01 / Explore the detail

Why the Portal Matters So Much

Think about it from the trader’s side. They’ve probably used a few brokers before. They know what a smooth sign-up feels like, and what it feels like to wait three days for a withdrawal with no updates.

A good portal makes your brokerage feel organised and trustworthy. A clumsy one makes even excellent execution look suspect. Traders reasonably assume that if the basics are messy, the rest might be too.

With a grey label, you run your own MetaTrader server, so your portal can connect to it directly. That makes it possible to build a far smoother experience than many white label setups allow.

02 / Explore the detail

Registration and Onboarding

The first few minutes count most. Good trader’s room software keeps registration short and gets clients to a funded account as quickly as your compliance rules allow.

01

Features to Look For

A short sign-up form, with extra details collected later rather than all at once

Social or email sign-up options where your regulator allows them

Mobile-friendly design, since many clients sign up from their phones

Clear progress steps so clients know what’s left to do

Language options for the markets you serve

02

KYC and Verification

Clients should be able to upload ID and proof of address straight from their phone camera. Automated checks can approve straightforward cases quickly and send unclear ones to your compliance team. The portal should also show clients exactly where their verification stands, so they aren’t left guessing or emailing support.

03 / Explore the detail

Account Management

Once verified, traders want control over their own accounts without having to contact anyone.

A good portal lets them:

Open new live or demo accounts instantly

Choose from the account types you offer, such as standard, raw spread or swap-free

Change leverage within the limits you’ve set

Reset MetaTrader passwords

See all their accounts, balances and equity in one place

Because a grey label gives you admin control over your server, these actions can sync to MetaTrader immediately. A new account opened in the portal is ready to trade within moments.

04 / Explore the detail

Deposits, Withdrawals and Transfers

This is where the portal earns its keep, and where most complaints start if things go wrong.

01

Deposits

Offer the payment methods your target markets actually use: cards, bank transfer, local e-wallets, and crypto where permitted. Deposits should show up in the client’s MetaTrader balance automatically once payment is confirmed. Every extra step between paying and seeing funds is a chance for a client to lose patience.

02

Withdrawals

Clients should be able to request a withdrawal in a few clicks, see its status clearly, and get notified at each stage. On your side, the back office should flag requests that need extra checks while letting routine ones go through quickly.

03

Internal Transfers

Traders with multiple accounts often want to move funds between them. Instant internal transfers are a small feature that clients really appreciate.

05 / Explore the detail

Trading Insights and Reports

Many traders like to see their performance outside MetaTrader. A portal can show:

Trade history and account statements

Profit and loss over custom periods

Deposit and withdrawal history

Downloadable reports for tax or personal records

Some brokers go further with simple analytics, such as win rates, average trade duration or most-traded instruments. It’s not essential, but it’s the kind of detail that makes a portal feel thoughtful.

06 / Explore the detail

Support and Communication

The portal is a natural home for support. Look for:

A ticket system where clients can follow their requests

Live chat linked to the client’s account details, so agents don’t have to ask for login numbers

A notification centre for important updates, such as margin warnings, new account types or scheduled maintenance

An FAQ or help section covering the questions your team gets asked again and again

Good support tools cut your workload too. Clients who can find answers themselves raise fewer tickets.

07 / Explore the detail

Features That Add Extra Value

Once the essentials are solid, extra features can set your portal apart.

01

Copy Trading and PAMM Access

If you offer copy trading or managed accounts, the portal is where clients browse strategy providers, check performance and choose who to follow. Investors should be able to see their allocations and results without logging into separate systems.

02

IB and Affiliate Areas

Introducing brokers need their own section to see their referred clients, trading volumes and commissions. A clear, accurate IB area helps you attract and keep good partners.

03

Education and Market Content

Some brokers put tutorials, market analysis, economic calendars or webinar sign-ups in the portal. It keeps clients coming back and gives newer traders a reason to stay with you as they learn.

08 / Explore the detail

What Your Team Needs Behind the Scenes

The client side gets the attention, but the back office matters just as much. Your team should be able to:

View a client’s full profile, accounts and trading activity in one place

Approve KYC, deposits and withdrawals with a clear audit trail

Move clients between groups or change conditions when needed

Pull reports for compliance and management

Set permissions so each team member only sees what they need

When your forex client portal and back office share data properly with your grey label server, your team spends less time chasing information and more time helping clients.

09 / Explore the detail

Choosing the Right Software

When comparing trader’s room software, a few questions sort the strong options from the weak:

Does it integrate directly with your MetaTrader grey label server in real time?

Can it be fully branded, including domain, colours and emails?

How well does it work on mobile?

Which payment providers does it already support?

Can it grow with you to cover copy trading, PAMM and IB programmes?

How are updates and new features handled?

Ask for a live demo connected to a test server. Go through it as a new client would, from sign-up to first withdrawal. You’ll spot problems that no feature list will tell you about.

10 / Explore the detail

Conclusion

Your trading server does the heavy lifting, but your client portal shapes how traders feel about your brokerage. Get registration, payments and account management right, and everything else becomes easier.

If you’re planning the client side of your grey label setup, MetaGreyLabel can help you choose and connect a portal that fits your markets and your traders.

Registration and Onboarding

Account Management

Deposits, Withdrawals and Transfers

Find the right components for your brokerage. Explore the options, then define a connected operating model.

Compare models →

The context

Your trading platform is where clients spend most of their time with you. It’s where they watch charts, place orders, test strategies and decide whether your brokerage feels reliable. If the platform lets them down, nothing else you offer will make up for it.

That’s why choosing the right forex trading platforms for brokers matters so much. We focus on MetaTrader, the platforms most traders already use and expect, and we give you every way to access them: desktop, web and mobile, all under your brand.

Choose your next step

Explore Trading Platforms (Main Room)

Web Trader

Not every client wants to download software. Some are on a work laptop where they can’t install anything. Some are using a borrowed computer. Some…

Explore Web Trader ↗

Mobile Trading App (iOS / Android)

Watch how most people trade now and you’ll notice something. The phone comes out first. They check positions over breakfast, react to news on the…

Explore Mobile Trading App (iOS / Android) ↗

Desktop Platform

Mobile and web trading are convenient, but when traders want to do real work, they sit down at a desktop. That’s where they run multiple charts side…

Explore Desktop Platform ↗

01 / Explore the detail

Why MetaTrader Is the Platform Traders Expect

There are plenty of trading platforms out there. MetaTrader remains the one most retail forex and CFD traders look for when choosing a broker.

01

Familiarity

Most traders have used MT4 or MT5 at some point. Offering it means there’s almost no learning curve. They can start trading the same day they fund their account.

02

A Huge Ecosystem

Thousands of indicators, expert advisors, scripts and signals are built for MetaTrader. Traders can bring their favourite tools with them, which is a big reason they choose one broker over another.

03

Proven Reliability

MetaTrader has been tested by millions of traders through every kind of market condition. Brokers and clients both know what to expect from it.

02 / Explore the detail

MT4 and MT5: Choosing Your Platform

We support both MetaTrader platforms, and many brokers offer the two side by side.

01

MT4

Built mainly for forex, MT4 is still loved by traders who rely on its huge library of indicators and EAs. It’s simple, stable and a strong choice if your audience is forex focused.

02

MT5

The newer platform supports forex alongside metals, energies, indices, stocks, futures and crypto CFDs. It offers more timeframes, more order types, market depth, an economic calendar and a much faster strategy tester. Most new brokers now lead with MT5.

03

Offering Both

Running both platforms lets every trader choose what they’re comfortable with. It widens your audience and removes one more reason for someone to look elsewhere.

03 / Explore the detail

MT4 MT5 Web Mobile Desktop: Trade Anywhere

Modern traders switch devices constantly. They analyse charts on a desktop at home, check positions on their phone during the day and sometimes log in from a browser on someone else’s computer. Offering MT4 MT5 web mobile desktop access means they can trade wherever they are.

01

Desktop Terminal

The full-featured version for serious analysis and automated trading. Advanced charting, custom indicators, expert advisors, multiple chart layouts and the strategy tester all live here.

02

WebTrader

Trade straight from a browser with no download needed. Ideal for clients who use shared or work computers, or who want quick access without installing software.

03

Mobile Apps for iOS and Android

Monitor positions, open and close trades, view charts and receive alerts on the go. For many clients, the mobile app is how they check in most often.

04

Synced Across Devices

Clients log in with the same account details on every device. Positions, balances and history stay consistent wherever they trade.

04 / Explore the detail

Your Brand on Every Platform

Your broker trading platform should look and feel like part of your business, not someone else’s.

01

Branded Terminals

Your logo, company name and server name appear across the platform, so clients always know who they’re trading with.

02

Branded Downloads and Links

Clients download your platform from your website and access WebTrader through your domain.

03

Consistent Experience

From the website to the trader’s room to the platform itself, clients move through your brand without confusing jumps between different looks and names.

05 / Explore the detail

How the Platform Connects to Everything Else

A trading platform doesn’t work in isolation. It sits at the centre of your brokerage, linked to every other system.

Your CRM opens accounts and syncs client data. Your trader’s room handles deposits, withdrawals and account management. Your liquidity bridge delivers prices and routes orders. Your back office and reporting tools pull trading data for finance, compliance and management. Your IB module calculates commissions from real trading activity.

With our setups, these connections are built and tested before you launch, so everything works together from the first trade.

06 / Explore the detail

Choosing How to Run Your Platform

How much control you have over your platform depends on the model you choose.

01

White Label

A branded platform on an existing server with limited control. Affordable and quick to launch.

02

Grey Label

Your own groups, trading conditions and manager access on an existing server. More independence without the cost of a full licence.

03

Admin Licence

Your own MetaTrader server, licensed in your name, with full administrator control.

We’ll help you choose the right option for your stage and budget, and you can move up as your brokerage grows.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I offer both MT4 and MT5 to my clients?

Yes. Many brokers run both platforms, and clients can open accounts on either one through the same trader’s room.

Do clients need to download anything to trade?

Not necessarily. They can use WebTrader directly in their browser, or download the desktop terminal or mobile app if they prefer.

Will the platform carry my branding?

Yes. Your company name and logo appear on the platform, and clients access it through your website and domain.

Can clients use their own indicators and expert advisors?

Yes. MetaTrader supports custom indicators and EAs on the desktop terminal. MT4 tools need to be built for MT4, and MT5 tools for MT5.

08 / Explore the detail

Give Your Traders the Platforms They Want

Traders choose brokers partly on the platforms they offer. Giving them trusted MetaTrader access on every device, under your brand, removes a major barrier to signing up.

Whether you’re comparing forex trading platforms for brokers, planning full MT4 MT5 web mobile desktop access, or setting up your first broker trading platform, we’ll help you get it right. Get in touch today.

Scope & responsibilities

Final modules and access depend on the agreed package.

The context

A grey label is a great place to grow. You’ve got your brand, your own groups and real control over trading conditions. But at some point, many brokers start to feel the ceiling. Volumes are up, the team is bigger, and the idea of running your own server, under your own licence, starts to sound less like a dream and more like the obvious next step.

If that’s where you are, this page explains what it means to upgrade grey label to admin level, what changes, what it costs in effort and money, and how we help you make the move without disrupting your clients.

01 / Operational scope

What an Admin License Actually Means

On a grey label, you work inside a server that’s licensed and controlled by your provider. You have manager access, but the deepest settings, server configuration and licence ownership stay with them.

With an admin licence, the server is yours. You hold the licence, you get full administrator access and you decide how every part of the environment is configured. Plugins, server settings, data feeds, gateways, backups, all of it.

01

The Practical Difference

On a grey label, you run your business on someone else’s platform. With an admin licence, the platform itself belongs to you. That brings more freedom, more responsibility and a stronger position when talking to banks, regulators and investors.

02 / Operational scope

Signs You’re Ready to Upgrade

Not every broker should make this move, and certainly not too early. Here are the signals that usually mean the timing is right.

01

Your Volumes Justify the Cost

When your monthly grey label fees, plus the revenue you’re leaving on the table, start to approach what owning your own server would cost, the maths begins to favour an upgrade.

02

You Need Deeper Customisation

Maybe you want plugins your provider can’t run, custom server-side logic, or integrations with tools that need administrator access. Those are hard to achieve on a grey label.

03

Regulators or Partners Expect It

Some licensing authorities, banking partners and institutional clients prefer, or require, that a broker owns its trading infrastructure. An admin licence can make those conversations much easier.

04

You Have the Team to Support It

Running your own server means taking on more technical responsibility. If you’ve got, or can hire, people who understand MetaTrader administration, you’re in a much better position to upgrade.

03 / Operational scope

MT4 Admin License Upgrade: How It Works

An MT4 admin license upgrade sounds complicated, and done badly, it can be. Done properly, your traders barely notice anything happened.

01

Planning

We start by mapping your current setup. Groups, symbols, trading conditions, plugins, CRM connections, payment flows and liquidity routes. Nothing gets moved until we know exactly what’s there.

02

Licensing and Server Setup

We guide you through acquiring your own licence and set up your new server environment, configured to match what you already run, plus any improvements you’ve been wanting.

03

Migration

Client accounts, history, balances and open positions are moved across, usually over a weekend when markets are closed. We test everything thoroughly before reopening.

04

Go Live and Handover

Your team gets full administrator access and training on what’s new. Our support continues afterwards, so you’re never left managing a new server alone.

04 / Operational scope

Grow From Grey Label to White Label: Clearing Up the Terms

You may see the phrase grow from grey label to white label and wonder if it’s backwards. It depends on who’s talking.

In everyday broker conversations, a white label usually means the lightest entry option, a branded platform on someone else’s server with limited control. That’s how we use it elsewhere on this site.

But MetaQuotes, the company behind MetaTrader, uses “White Label” to describe its full branded server licence. In that sense, growing from a grey label to a white label means moving to your own licensed server, which is exactly what this page is about.

01

Why the Confusion Matters

If a provider offers you a “white label upgrade,” ask exactly what you’ll own. Is it a full licence in your company’s name with administrator access? Or a branded platform on their server with less control than you have now? The answer changes everything.

05 / Operational scope

What You Gain After Upgrading

Full control over server configuration and plugins. Ownership of your licence and trading infrastructure. Freedom to choose your own hosting, data centres and technology partners. A stronger profile with regulators, banks and investors. And no ceiling on how far you can customise your brokerage.

01

What You Take On

More responsibility for uptime, security and maintenance. Higher upfront licence costs. A need for in-house or outsourced technical expertise. We’ll be honest about all of this, because an upgrade only makes sense if you’re ready for both sides of it.

06 / Operational scope

How We Support Your Upgrade

Because we already know your grey label setup inside out, we’re well placed to handle the move. We plan the migration, set up and configure your new server, transfer your clients and data, and stay on as your technical partner afterwards if you’d like us to.

Some clients keep us on for full server management. Others take most of it in-house and use us for specialist support. Either works.

07 / Operational scope

Ready to Own Your Infrastructure?

If your brokerage has outgrown shared infrastructure, it may be time to upgrade grey label to admin and take full ownership of your platform.

Whether you’re planning an MT4 admin license upgrade or exploring what it means to grow from grey label to white label under MetaQuotes’ licensing, we’ll walk you through the costs, the timeline and the risks honestly. Tell us where your brokerage is today, and we’ll help you plan the next step. Get in touch.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does an upgrade to an admin licence take?

It depends on the licensing process and the size of your setup. The migration itself is usually done over a weekend, but planning and licence approval can take several weeks. We’ll give you a realistic timeline at the start.

Will my clients notice the change?

If it’s planned well, very little. Accounts, balances and history move across, and clients log in to a new server address. We help you communicate the change clearly so nobody is caught off guard.

Can I upgrade from MT5 as well as MT4?

Yes. While this page focuses on the MT4 admin licence upgrade, we support the same move for MT5 brokers, or for brokers running both platforms.

Do I need my own technical team after upgrading?

You’ll need someone responsible for server administration. That can be an in-house team, us, or a mix of both. We’ll help you decide what makes sense for your size.

The context

Not every client wants to download software. Some are on a work laptop where they can’t install anything. Some are using a borrowed computer. Some just want to check a position quickly without opening a full desktop terminal. For all of them, a web-based platform is the easiest way in.

An MT4 web trader or MT5 web trader lets your clients trade straight from their browser. No downloads, no installation, no compatibility headaches. They open a link, log in and they’re trading, all under your brand.

01 / Explore the detail

What Is a Web Trader?

A web trader is a version of MetaTrader that runs entirely inside an internet browser. It connects to the same server and accounts as the desktop and mobile apps, so clients see the same balances, positions and history wherever they log in.

01

Same Account, Different Doorway

Clients don’t need a separate account for web trading. They use the same login details they use on desktop or mobile.

02

Works on Most Devices

Windows, Mac, Linux or Chromebook. If the device has a modern browser, it can run the web trader.

02 / Explore the detail

Why Web Trading Matters for Your Brokerage

01

Faster Onboarding

New clients can place their first trade minutes after funding, without a download step that some people abandon halfway through.

02

Fewer Support Requests

No installation problems, no “the app won’t open on my Mac” emails. The browser handles it.

03

Easy Access for Casual Traders

Newer or less technical traders often find a browser platform less intimidating than a full desktop terminal.

04

Always Up to Date

Clients don’t need to install updates. When the web platform improves, everyone gets the latest version automatically.

03 / Explore the detail

MT4 Web Trader

The MT4 web trader brings the core of MT4 into the browser. It’s a good fit for forex-focused brokerages whose clients already know MT4.

01

What Clients Can Do

View live prices, open and close trades, set stop loss and take profit levels, manage pending orders, view account history and use a selection of built-in indicators and chart tools.

02

Where It Fits

It’s ideal for quick trading and position management. Traders who rely heavily on custom indicators or expert advisors will still want the desktop terminal for that work.

04 / Explore the detail

MT5 Web Trader

The MT5 web trader offers a richer browser experience, with more instruments, more timeframes and more analysis tools.

01

What Clients Can Do

Trade forex, metals, indices, commodities, stocks and other instruments you offer. Use more chart types and timeframes, view market depth on supported symbols, and manage orders with a wider range of order types.

02

Where It Fits

It suits multi-asset brokerages and clients who want a fuller trading experience without installing software.

05 / Explore the detail

White Label Web Trading Platform: Your Brand in the Browser

A white label web trading platform should feel like part of your brokerage, not a third-party tool clients are sent off to use.

01

Hosted on Your Domain

Clients access the web trader through a link on your website or a subdomain you control, keeping them inside your brand.

02

Your Branding

Your company name and logo appear where the platform allows, and your server name shows at login, so clients know exactly who they’re trading with.

03

Linked From the Trader’s Room

Clients can jump from the client portal straight into the web trader with one click, making the whole journey feel connected.

06 / Explore the detail

Benefits of a Browser Trading Platform for Clients

From the client’s side, a browser trading platform is simply convenient.

01

No Installation

Nothing to download or set up. Open a browser, log in and start trading.

02

Trade From Anywhere

Home computer, office laptop, hotel business centre. Any device with a browser works.

03

Consistent With Other Devices

Positions opened on mobile show up in the browser instantly, and vice versa.

04

Secure Connection

Data travels over encrypted connections, and clients log in with the same secure credentials they use elsewhere.

07 / Explore the detail

How It Fits With Desktop and Mobile

The web trader works best as one part of a complete platform offering. Most active traders end up using a mix. Desktop for deep analysis and automated strategies, mobile for checking in throughout the day, and web for quick access when they’re away from their usual setup.

Offering all three, under one brand and one account, is what clients now expect from a serious brokerage.

08 / Explore the detail

Set Up as Part of Your Brokerage

With our white label, grey label and turnkey packages, web trading access is configured alongside your desktop and mobile platforms. We link it to your website and trader’s room, apply your branding and test it across common browsers before launch.

09 / Explore the detail

Let Clients Trade the Moment They’re Ready

A web trader removes one more barrier between a new client and their first trade. It’s quick, easy and works almost anywhere.

Whether you want an MT4 web trader, an MT5 web trader, or a fully branded white label web trading platform, we’ll set up a reliable browser trading platform your clients can access from any device. Get in touch today.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Frequently Asked Questions

Do clients need a separate account for the web trader?

No. Clients log in with the same account details they use on the desktop terminal and mobile apps.

Can clients use expert advisors on the web trader?

Expert advisors and most custom indicators run on the desktop terminal, not in the browser. The web trader is designed for manual trading and position management.

Which browsers does the web trader support?

It works on most modern browsers, including Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge. We test across these before launch.

Can I offer both MT4 and MT5 web traders?

Yes. If you run both platforms, clients can access each through the browser using the matching account.

White Label, Grey Label or Turnkey? Choosing the Right Model

Practical perspectives on brokerage technology and operations.

5 min read · Meta Grey Label

The context

Spend a little time researching how to start a brokerage and you’ll run into three terms over and over: white label, grey label and turnkey. They’re often presented as three options on the same menu. They aren’t, quite. White label and grey label describe how you access the trading platform. Turnkey describes how much of the whole business comes ready-made.

Once you see it that way, the choice gets much easier. Here’s how the three fit together, and how to work out which one suits your plans.

01 / Explore the detail

White Label: Renting a Branded Space

A white label puts your brand on a MetaTrader server that someone else runs. You share that server with other brokers, and the host controls the core configuration. You get a manager terminal, branded client terminals and the ability to open accounts and manage clients.

It’s the quickest and cheapest way to get a platform running. The trade-off is limited control over liquidity, execution settings, plugins and data. For brokers testing a market or working with a very tight budget, that trade-off is often worth it.

02 / Explore the detail

Grey Label: Your Own Server, Someone Else’s License

A grey label gives you a dedicated MetaTrader server running under your provider’s master license. You get admin access, so you configure groups, symbols, swaps and execution yourself. You pick your liquidity providers, add the plugins you want, and your client data sits on your own server.

It costs more than a white label and needs more technical know-how to run, but it gives you far more freedom. Many brokers move to a grey label once they’ve outgrown a white label, while others start there because they already have the experience and client base to use the extra control.

03 / Explore the detail

Turnkey: The Whole Business in One Package

A turnkey forex broker solution is about scope rather than platform access. Instead of buying the trading server alone and sourcing everything else separately, you get most of what you need to launch from one provider.

A typical turnkey package might include:

The trading platform, on either a white label or grey label basis

A forex CRM and branded client portal

Liquidity access and a bridge

Payment gateway integrations

Risk management and back office tools

Website design and development

Help with company formation and licensing

Ongoing technical support

The idea is simple: one contract, one point of contact and one integrated stack, rather than six vendors who have never worked together.

04 / Explore the detail

How They Combine

Here’s where people get confused. Turnkey isn’t a third type of platform. It’s a package that sits on top of one.

So you might come across a white label turnkey solution, which is fast and inexpensive with limited control. Or you might choose a metatrader grey label turnkey setup, where you get your own server with admin access plus the CRM, bridge, payments and website already connected around it.

The second option is popular with brokers who want real control over their trading environment but don’t want to spend months stitching together tools from different suppliers.

05 / Explore the detail

Weighing Up the Options

01

If Speed and Low Cost Come First

A white label, possibly as part of a basic turnkey bundle, gets you live fastest with the smallest upfront spend. It’s a reasonable way to test demand, learn the business and build an initial client base.

Just go in knowing you’ll probably outgrow it, and check how easy it is to move on later.

02

If Control Matters Most

A grey label gives you control over execution, liquidity and configuration. If you have an experienced team and clear views on how you want to run your book, sourcing each component yourself lets you pick the best tool for every job.

That said, it takes time and technical effort, and you become the one responsible for making everything talk to everything else.

03

If You Want Control Without the Assembly

A grey label turnkey package is the middle path. You keep the server control that makes a grey label worthwhile, while your provider handles integration and delivers a working brokerage instead of a box of parts.

For many first-time brokers with a solid budget, this is the most practical route. It’s also common among established businesses expanding into forex from related fields, such as crypto exchanges or financial education companies, who know their audience but not brokerage technology.

06 / Explore the detail

Questions That Point You the Right Way

Answering these honestly usually settles the choice:

How much capital do you have for setup and your first year of running costs?

Does your team include people who have run a MetaTrader server before?

Do you already have liquidity relationships, or do you need introductions?

How quickly do you need to launch?

Do you already own any parts of the stack, like a CRM or website, that you want to keep?

How much control do you need over execution and risk from day one?

If you’re short on time, technical staff and existing tools, turnkey makes sense. If you have strong opinions and an experienced team, assembling your own stack around a grey label may suit you better.

07 / Explore the detail

What to Watch For With Turnkey Packages

Turnkey solutions can be excellent, but they come with their own risks:

Lock-in: if everything comes from one provider, leaving can be harder. Check whether you can swap out individual components later.

Hidden weak spots: a package might include an excellent platform but a mediocre CRM. Assess each part, not just the overall bundle.

Vague licensing help: “assistance with licensing” can mean anything from a full application service to a list of law firms. Ask exactly what’s included.

Bundled pricing: ask for a breakdown so you can see what each part really costs.

08 / Explore the detail

There’s No Permanent Choice

Plenty of brokers start on one model and switch later. A white label turnkey can become a grey label as the business grows. A grey label turnkey can be gradually unbundled as you bring parts of the stack in-house. What matters is choosing something that fits where you are now, with a clear route to where you want to be.

09 / Explore the detail

Conclusion

White label and grey label decide how much control you have over your trading server. Turnkey decides how much of the rest of the business arrives ready to go. A turnkey forex broker setup built on a grey label gives many brokers the best of both: real control and a much faster, simpler launch.

If you’re weighing up a metatrader grey label turnkey option, MetaGreyLabel can talk you through what would be included and how it would fit your plans.

White Label Pricing

Understand setup, ongoing service and optional modules before choosing your scope.

Discuss your requirements ↗

Compare models →

The context

Pricing is usually the first thing brokers want to know and the last thing most providers explain clearly. You’ll often see “contact us for a quote” and nothing else. That makes it hard to plan a budget, let alone compare options.

So this page lays it out properly. What goes into a forex white label price, what you pay upfront, what you pay each month and what’s optional. By the end, you should have a good idea of where your setup is likely to land before you ever pick up the phone.

01 / Explore the detail

What Makes Up White Label Forex Cost?

Every brokerage is a little different, but the white label forex cost almost always breaks down into the same few parts.

01

The One-Time Setup Fee

This covers getting you live. Server configuration, branding the platform, creating your account groups and symbols, connecting your back office and testing everything before launch. You pay it once.

02

The Monthly Fee

This keeps everything running. Server access, hosting, platform updates, maintenance and support from our team. It’s a fixed amount each month, agreed upfront.

03

Optional Add-Ons

Extra tools you can bolt on when you need them. Copy trading, PAMM and MAM accounts, additional payment gateways, advanced risk management plugins and so on. Nothing here is forced on you at launch.

02 / Explore the detail

Understanding the White Label Setup Fee

The white label setup fee is the part people tend to worry about most, mainly because some providers use it to hide a lot of extra charges. Ours covers a clearly defined list of work.

01

What the Setup Fee Includes

Branding the trading terminal across desktop, web and mobile. Setting up your account groups, leverage, symbols and commission structure. Connecting the platform to your CRM and client portal. Integrating your chosen payment methods. Testing everything with your team before go live.

02

What Can Push It Higher

A few things add work and therefore cost. Running both MT4 and MT5 rather than one platform. A large number of custom symbols or complex group structures. Custom website design instead of a template. Integrations with third-party tools you already use.

We’ll flag any of these early, so the quote you approve is the quote you pay.

03 / Explore the detail

Our White Label Packages

Most brokers fit into one of three broad packages. Each can be adjusted, but they give you a realistic starting point.

01

Starter Package

Setup fee: [price] Monthly fee: [price]

Built for brokers testing a market or moving from IB to their own brand. Includes a branded MT4 or MT5 platform, basic back office access, standard account groups and email support. Simple, affordable and quick to launch.

02

Growth Package

Setup fee: [price] Monthly fee: [price]

Our most popular option. Adds a forex CRM with KYC, a trader’s room for deposits and withdrawals, payment gateway integration, an IB module and priority support. This is where most serious new brokerages start.

03

Turnkey Package

Setup fee: [price] Monthly fee: [price]

Everything in one place. Branded platform, full CRM, client portal, multiple payment gateways, IB module, branded website and dedicated account contacts. Built for founders who want a complete brokerage without managing multiple suppliers.

04 / Explore the detail

MT4 White Label Pricing Compared With MT5

Brokers often ask whether MT4 white label pricing differs from MT5. In most cases the gap is small, and the bigger cost difference comes from what you build around the platform rather than the platform itself.

01

When MT4 Makes Sense

If your audience is mainly forex traders who already use MT4 indicators and EAs, it’s a sensible choice and keeps things familiar for them.

02

When MT5 Makes Sense

If you plan to offer indices, commodities, stocks or crypto CFDs, MT5 handles all of it in one terminal. It also tends to be the better long-term pick for new brokerages.

03

Running Both

Offering both platforms adds some configuration work and a higher monthly fee, but it widens your audience. Plenty of brokers decide it’s worth it once they see how many traders care about platform choice.

05 / Explore the detail

Costs to Plan for Outside the White Label

Your technology is one part of the budget. To give you an honest picture, here are other costs brokers commonly need to plan for. These come from third parties, not from us.

Company registration and licensing, which vary widely by jurisdiction. Legal and compliance advice. Liquidity provider minimum deposits or fees. Payment processor setup and transaction fees. Marketing to bring in your first clients.

We can point you towards trusted partners for several of these, but we’d rather you know about them now than discover them later.

06 / Explore the detail

How We Keep Pricing Honest

A lot of brokers come to us after unpleasant surprises with other providers. A cheap monthly rate that slowly grew through extra charges for reports, plugin access, configuration changes or support hours.

We work differently. Every cost in your setup is listed in the proposal before you sign. Routine configuration changes are part of your monthly fee. If you ever need something outside your package, we’ll quote it first and you decide.

01

Pay for What You Use Now

You don’t need every feature on day one. Start with what your brokerage actually needs and add tools as your volumes and team grow. Your costs rise in line with your revenue, not ahead of it.

07 / Explore the detail

Get a Clear Quote for Your Brokerage

The easiest way to pin down your exact forex white label price is a short conversation. Tell us your target markets, expected client numbers, preferred platform and which features matter most to you. We’ll send back a detailed proposal with every line explained.

Whether you’re comparing MT4 white label pricing, trying to understand the full white label forex cost, or simply want to know what the white label setup fee covers before you commit, we’ll give you a straight answer. Get in touch today.

White Label vs Grey Label

Compare the operating choices, responsibilities and trade-offs before you decide.

Discuss your requirements ↗

Compare models →

Choose your operating model

Control. Scope. Responsibility.

White label

Provider-led platform operations.

Grey label

More direct manager-level control.

Start with what your team needs to manage directly. Confirm the commercial and technical scope before launch.

Explore the decision criteria ↓

The context

Ask ten people in this industry to explain the difference and you’ll probably get ten slightly different answers. Some providers use the terms loosely. Others blur them on purpose to make a cheaper package sound like more than it is.

That’s a problem when you’re about to commit real money. This page breaks down white label vs grey label in plain language, so you can see what each model gives you, what it costs you in control, and which one makes more sense for where your brokerage is right now.

A white label lets you trade under your own brand on someone else’s MetaTrader server, with limited control over how that server is run.

A grey label also runs on an existing server, but you get your own manager access and much more say over trading conditions, groups and risk.

Both are far cheaper than buying a full MetaTrader licence. The real question is how much independence you need today.

01 / Explore the detail

The Difference Between White Label and Grey Label Forex

To understand the difference between white label and grey label forex setups properly, it helps to look at a few specific areas.

Control Over Trading Conditions

White label

On a white label, many of your settings sit under the main server’s oversight. You may be able to set some spreads and commissions, but leverage limits, symbol settings and group structures are often restricted.

Grey label

On a grey label, those decisions are largely yours. You can build your own groups, set your own spreads and markups, adjust leverage and decide which instruments each client type can trade.

Manager and Admin Access

White label

White label brokers usually get a limited back office view. Enough to see clients and accounts, but not much more.

Grey label

Grey label brokers get proper manager terminal access. Your dealing team can monitor exposure, adjust positions, manage groups and react to market conditions without waiting on anyone else.

Risk Management

White label

This is one of the biggest practical differences. With a white label, risk is often handled at the main server level, which limits how you can run your book.

Grey label

With a grey label, you have far more flexibility. You can decide how much flow to route to liquidity providers, how much to keep internally and how to treat different client groups. For brokers who want to grow revenue seriously, that matters a lot.

Branding

Both models / commercial scope

Both models let you put your name on the platform, the client portal and your website. Traders won’t see the provider behind you in either case. Branding isn’t really where they differ.

Cost

Both models / commercial scope

A white label is the cheaper option, both in setup fee and monthly fee. A grey label costs more because you’re getting more control and more server resources. Even so, both sit well below the cost of a full licence and your own infrastructure.

Speed to Launch

Both models / commercial scope

Both can go live quickly once your paperwork is ready. A white label is sometimes a little faster simply because there’s less to configure.

02 / Explore the detail

When a White Label Makes Sense

A white label is a smart choice when you want to get started with minimal risk and keep early costs low.

It fits introducing brokers taking their first step towards their own brand, founders testing whether a particular market will respond, and businesses adding forex as a side offering rather than a core product. If you don’t yet have a dealing team or a clear risk strategy, a white label also takes a lot of that pressure off.

The trade-off is control. Once your client numbers grow, the restrictions usually start to feel tight.

03 / Explore the detail

When a Grey Label Makes Sense

A grey label suits brokers who already know their market and want room to run things their own way.

It works well if you have steady client volumes, a team that understands dealing and risk, or plans to fine-tune spreads and conditions for different client types. It’s also the natural step for white label brokers who’ve outgrown their setup but aren’t ready for the cost of a full licence.

You get much of the independence of owning a server, without the heavy infrastructure bill.

04 / Explore the detail

White Label vs Grey Label: Which Is Better for Brokers?

There’s no universal answer to which is better for brokers, and anyone who tells you otherwise is probably trying to sell you one in particular. It really depends on your stage, your team and your budget.

01

Ask Yourself a Few Questions

How many active clients do you expect in your first year? Do you have someone who can manage a dealing desk? Do you need custom groups and trading conditions from day one, or can that wait? How much are you comfortable spending upfront before you’ve proven the model?

If most of your answers lean towards “not yet,” a white label is probably the right start. If you’ve already got clients, a team and a clear plan, a grey label will likely serve you better.

02

You Don’t Have to Decide Forever

This is the part people often miss. Starting on one model doesn’t lock you in. Plenty of our clients launch as a white label, prove their market, then move to a grey label within a year or two. Because both run on the same infrastructure with us, the switch is smooth and your clients barely notice.

05 / Explore the detail

How We Help You Choose

We’d honestly rather you pick the right model than the more expensive one. A broker on the wrong setup either overpays for control they don’t use or gets frustrated by limits they’ve outgrown. Neither is good for a long relationship.

So our first conversation focuses on your plans. Your markets, your expected volumes, your team and your budget. From there we’ll recommend the model that fits, explain why, and show you exactly what it costs.

Answers, without the ambiguity

Still Weighing White Label vs Grey Label?

The white label vs grey label decision is one of the most important you’ll make early on, and it’s worth getting a second opinion before you commit.

Can my clients tell whether I’m on a white label or a grey label?

No. In both cases, traders see your brand on the platform, the client portal and your website. The difference is in how much control you have behind the scenes, not in what your clients see when they log in.

Is a grey label much more expensive than a white label?

It costs more, both in setup and monthly fees, because you’re getting manager access, more server resources and greater control over trading conditions. That said, both models are still far cheaper than buying a full MetaTrader licence and running your own infrastructure.

How long does it take to move from a white label to a grey label?

Usually not long, as both run on the same infrastructure with us. We plan the switch around your trading hours, move your groups and client accounts across, and test everything before it goes live. Most clients barely notice the change.

Do I need a licence for either model?

That depends on where you’re based and which markets you want to serve. Some jurisdictions require a licence before you accept clients, whichever model you choose. We can share what we’ve seen work for other brokers, but your legal advisor should confirm what applies to you.

Why Choose Us

The people, principles and technical work behind a connected brokerage.

Discuss your requirements ↗

Compare models →

The context

There’s no shortage of companies offering to launch your forex brokerage. Search for a few minutes and you’ll find dozens, all promising speed, low costs and round-the-clock support. Most of them sound exactly the same.

So it’s a fair question. Why choose MetaTrader Grey Label over everyone else? We’d rather show you than tell you, so here’s a plain breakdown of what you actually get when you work with us.

01 / Explore the detail

Launch Speed That Holds Up in Practice

Fast setup is easy to promise. Delivering it every time is harder.

Because our MetaTrader infrastructure is already built and tested, we’re not starting from a blank server when you sign up. Most of the work is configuring what already exists around your brand, your groups and your trading conditions. That’s why a standard setup can go live in a couple of days once your documents are in order.

When something on your side will slow things down, like a pending licence or a payment provider still reviewing your application, we tell you early. You won’t find out about delays the night before your planned launch.

02 / Explore the detail

Pricing That Respects a New Broker’s Budget

Money is tight when you’re starting out. Every dollar spent on technology is a dollar not spent on marketing, compliance or hiring.

We’ve built our packages with that in mind. If you’ve been hunting for the lowest pricing forex broker setup that doesn’t cut corners, this is where we tend to stand out. You pay for what you need now, not for features you might use in two years.

01

No Hidden Costs Buried in the Contract

A lot of brokers come to us after getting burned by add-on fees. A low monthly price on the website, then extra charges for plugins, reports, server changes and support hours. We list what each part of your setup costs before you sign. If something changes later, you’ll hear about it first.

02

Pay As You Grow

Start with the essentials. Add a more advanced CRM, extra liquidity connections or copy trading tools once your client base justifies them. Your costs scale with your business instead of running ahead of it.

03 / Explore the detail

Real Control Over Your Brokerage

With a basic white label, you’re often stuck with someone else’s spreads, groups and risk settings. That’s fine for testing an idea, but it gets frustrating once you have real clients.

Our grey label setups give you manager access and room to make your own decisions. You set leverage, symbols, commissions and client groups. Your dealing team can act quickly without waiting on another company’s approval.

01

Your Brand, Front and Centre

Clients see your name, your platform branding and your website. Not ours. It’s your business, and it should look like it.

04 / Explore the detail

Support From People Who Know MetaTrader Inside Out

This is the reason many brokers switch to us, and honestly, it’s the part we’re proudest of.

Plenty of providers have a support desk. Fewer have people on that desk who understand MT4 and MT5 at the server level. When your bridge drops during a news release or a report won’t generate before a compliance deadline, you need someone who can diagnose it quickly, not someone reading from a script.

01

Direct Contacts, Not Endless Tickets

You’ll have named people on our team who know your setup. They remember what was configured, what was changed last month and what your priorities are. That saves time on every single conversation.

02

Help That Continues After Launch

Go live day isn’t the finish line. We stay involved with updates, new integrations and adjustments as your brokerage grows.

05 / Explore the detail

Everything Works Together

A brokerage runs on a lot of moving parts. Trading platform, CRM, client portal, liquidity bridge, payment gateways, risk tools. When each comes from a different vendor, small mismatches turn into daily headaches. Deposits don’t show up. Client data doesn’t sync. Reports don’t match.

We set up and test these pieces as one system. It’s not glamorous work, but it’s the difference between running a business and spending your mornings fixing data errors.

06 / Explore the detail

What Makes Someone the Best Forex Technology Provider?

Every company in this space calls itself the best forex technology provider. The label doesn’t mean much on its own. What matters is what the provider does when things get difficult.

In our view, it comes down to a few things. Can they get you live without endless delays? Are their prices clear? Do they pick up when you call? Will they still care about your account six months after you’ve paid?

Those are the standards we hold ourselves to. We’d encourage you to ask every provider you’re considering the same questions, including us.

01

Honest Advice, Even When It Costs Us a Sale

Sometimes a broker asks for a full turnkey package when a simpler grey label would do the job better for now. We’ll say so. Sometimes a feature won’t suit their jurisdiction. We’ll say that too. Clients who get straight advice early tend to stay with us for years, and that’s worth far more than a bigger first invoice.

Built for Brokers at Every Stage

Our clients range quite a bit. First-time founders testing a single market. Introducing brokers ready to run their own book. Established firms launching a second brand in a new region. The setup looks different for each of them, but the approach stays the same. Understand the business first, then build the technology around it.

08 / Explore the detail

Ready to See the Difference for Yourself?

If you’re comparing providers right now, we’d genuinely like to be on your shortlist. Tell us what you’re building, your timeline and your budget, and we’ll put together a clear proposal with no pressure attached.

Looking for the best forex technology provider for your needs and the lowest pricing forex broker setup you can rely on? That’s a conversation worth having. And once you’ve spoken with our team, the answer to why choose MetaTrader Grey Label will probably feel a lot more obvious. Get in touch today.
